### Round 3: the game's review

The Settings switch (Settings → Workers → Prompt secrets), the review dialog and the send flow of the P overlay, the
laptop's prompt box and a paste into its terminal. Code: `game/src/world/promptSecrets.ts` (the switch, a scan read
strictly, the review's model), `game/src/ui/secretsFlow.ts` (the one send flow; round 4 plugs the other composers in),
`game/src/ui/secretsReview.ts` (the dialog), `game/src/ui/promptSecretsSection.ts`, `game/tools/fixture-secrets.ts`.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 26 | Order | On Send: the composer's resolved text (image markers and file paths in place: exactly what `worker.prompt` carries, so the UTF-16 ranges line up) is scanned first, before pack up's check or anything else reads it. Nothing found: today's send, no `secrets`, no dialog. Found: the review; nothing goes before Confirm. Off (or a bridge without the switch): today's send, no scan. |
| 27 | The dialog | The whole prompt in one scrolling monospace well, white space, line ends, tabs and Unicode as typed; a desk dialog as tall as the prompt needs (a screen-filling one for a long prompt: the plan-limits plate steps aside). Each match is a highlight at its exact boundaries with its decision on label-maker tape stuck before it: "Protected" (warning tape, solid edge, a wash) or "Ignored" (grey tape, dashed edge, no wash): text and shape, never colour alone. The tape sits in the line (it is visibly not prompt text, and never inside a value): a column can shift on that line, never a boundary. One strip under the well is about the match in hand (previous/next, Protect as file / Ignore this occurrence, Start and End one character either way, Mark the selection as secret, Remove this mark) rather than a popover per match: always under the well, the same for keyboard and touch. The counts and "Ignored matches are sent as plain text" sit in the footer beside Confirm and send and Cancel (Esc, the close button), so they are never scrolled away (what the last action did, when there is something to say, gets its own row above them). **A short screen** (under 480 px high: a laptop at 200% zoom, a phone on its side) tightens the header, body and footer, and the strip takes three rows instead of five when it is narrow too; the body scrolls between the header and the footer (the desk dialogs' idiom), so the prompt keeps three lines and every control of the strip is reached by scrolling, by wheel, touch or the focus. Fix round U1: at 640x360 the body did not scroll and cut the strip off behind the footer; `e2e/h108-prompt-secrets.spec.ts` checks at 1280x720, 640x360 and 390x844 (touch) that no control is cut off by a box that does not scroll, each is on top once scrolled to, and the counts and the footer are in view throughout. |
| 28 | Keys | The current match is one tab stop (roving); N and Shift+N step through the matches round the end and scroll the full prompt to them; Space or Enter on a match protects or ignores it (never submits: Confirm is its own button, Ctrl/⌘+Enter); ← → move its end, Shift+← → its start, a code point at a time, never into a neighbour or to nothing; M marks the selection; Delete takes a mark you made away. Ctrl/⌘+Shift+X in a prompt box (or its "Review secrets") opens the review on purpose, also when nothing is found, so a value the scan missed can be marked. All listed in `docs/shortcuts.md`. |
| 29 | Selecting text | The prompt is a `contenteditable` that refuses every edit (`beforeinput`, paste, drop, cut; a composition the platform does not let us refuse is put back): it is there for the native caret, so Shift+arrows select by keyboard and a touch selects with the platform's handles (`inputmode="none"`: no on-screen keyboard). A selection maps back to UTF-16 offsets through its text nodes (the tapes have none), its edges moved out of a surrogate pair. A mark over a match, ignored ones included, is refused with why (the match's edges are corrected instead). |
| 30 | What a decision carries | A protected candidate is sent with its range, corrected or not (the bridge takes the candidate's own range as such, and its retry identity is the protected ranges), so the command log can mask exactly what goes to files. Ignored: by id. Ignoring corrects nothing: an ignored match is its found range, as typed. **So Ignore is unavailable while another mark covers part of that found range** (a mark of yours over a character a correction freed, or a neighbour's edge moved into it): the strip's Ignore is shown unavailable with why in its title, and a press, a tap, Space or Enter says why too (your mark: take it away; match N: move its edge back) and changes nothing. A correction can take a match clear of where it was found (its end out, then its start after it: the edges are not bounded by the found range), and a mark in the gap does not cover the found range: Ignore passes over it, and the match is back in its place in the text. **Every range change goes through one step that keeps the marks in text order**, apart, non-empty and on code point boundaries (an edge stops at the next mark, a mark over another is refused, a stale review takes over only what still fits), so the prompt is drawn exactly as typed, the pending row and the command log mask exactly the protected ranges, and the decisions never overlap (`promptSecrets.test.ts` checks all of that after every step of random sequences that move matches clear of their found ranges and mark the gaps). Fix rounds C1: Ignore put a shrunk match back over the mark beside it (the prompt drew that character twice, the bridge refused the review); then back past a mark in the gap, out of text order (the prompt drawn twice over, a protected value in clear in the pending row, an edge moved into the mark). A review that decides nothing (no candidates, no marks) is no review: the prompt goes without `secrets`. |
| 31 | Refusals | `secrets_review_stale` and `secrets_review_required`: scanned and reviewed again with a note, the earlier choices taken over where the candidate is the same, sent only on a new Confirm (also when the new scan finds nothing: the review opens anyway). `secrets_review_off`: back to the composer, the draft kept, a note; `secrets_unavailable`: the same, as an error. A switch change while the dialog is open closes it: nothing sent, the reason said. Never an automatic send. |
| 32 | Retry | A send whose answer never came (a timeout, a dropped connection) keeps its review in memory: Send again of the same text to the same worker carries the same revision and decisions (no scan, no dialog: the bridge reuses the files it wrote). Any answer, or other text, drops it. |
| 33 | Raw text stays in memory | While the switch is on, the laptop's prompt box keeps its drafts in memory only: nothing is written to localStorage, a draft stored before is removed once it is read, and switching on removes the live drafts' stored copies at once (off: today's behaviour, written again). The P overlay's drafts were memory only already. The command log (`App.sent`, `window.__h3d.sent()`) keeps a scan's length, never its text, and a reviewed prompt's text with every protected range as `•` (lengths kept). The laptop's pending row shows each protected value as `[secret]` until the ack, then the ack's `sent` with its references. The review dialog empties its well when it closes. |
| 34 | Pack up (until round 4) | A prompt whose review protects anything skips pack up's check: `packup.detect` is an LLM call and would read the value (round 4 gives it the text with the references). Nothing found, or everything ignored, is plain text: the check runs as before. Known seam for round 4: "Send and go home" then sends `worker.wrapup`, which round 2 gates; with possible secrets in it the bridge will refuse it until round 4 wires that route. |
| 35 | A paste into a terminal | A paste to an agent is reviewed before it joins the worker's input lane (keys typed before it go first; the modal has the keyboard meanwhile); Confirm puts it in the lane, Cancel drops it ("Not pasted"). A plain shell takes keys, as before: there is no review for typed input (row 15). **No review on demand**: a paste in which the scan finds nothing goes as typed. A terminal has no prompt box for a "Review secrets" control, and Ctrl/⌘+Shift+X there is the terminal's ctrl+x; the user chose (2026-10-18, review C2) to state the limit rather than take a terminal chord or arm a "review the next paste" mode (round 4 may revisit). To mark a value the scan missed, send it from the P overlay or the laptop's prompt box instead. Settings says so in its limit sentence. |

"Confirm and send" for everything else. The check's applying is decided before the review opens (`packupAction`), so the word says what Confirm does. |

A refusal reviews again each text that has a candidate now or had decisions before (its choices taken over), never parsing the path out of the message. The retry memory is keyed by the command's key and every text. `run.start` sends `extra`'s review only beside no edited `prompt` (the bridge reads `extra` in the composed prompt only). ### Round 5: revoke, leases and the lifecycle

The files' lifecycle beyond round 1's: the explicit revoke, `Worker.secret_files`, the lease of a handoff's files to its
successor, and the lifecycle's tests; code in `internal/secretfiles` (`Lease`, `Release`/`ReleaseExpired`/`Sweep` with
liveness, `Revoke`, `Revoked`), `internal/store/promptsecrets.go` (`prompt_secret_lease`, `prompt_secret_handoff`,
`SecretFileCounts`) and `internal/server/promptsecretlifecycle.go`; the protocol in `docs/protocol.md` "Prompt secrets" →
"Round 5: revoke, leases and the lifecycle". Rows are numbered from 46: rounds 3 and 4 (the game) take 26–45.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 50 | Explicit revoke (the contract round 4's game control is built against) | **`prompt_secrets.revoke {"worker"}` → `{"removed": n}`**: every file the worker holds now, its own and those it holds by a lease, goes with its rows, for every holder; the worker keeps running and its earlier prompts keep references that point at nothing. With the switch on or off (turning it off never ended a file's lifecycle). `not_found` for a worker the bridge neither shows nor finds a file of; one of an asleep floor is shown, and one it does not show that holds files (of a herdr session that is gone, one its floor runs without: row 56) is revoked the same way (fix round, review L1: a worker that holds files must be revocable; the lifecycle keeps a gone session's files for its return, an explicit revoke removes them; round 4's game offers revoke only on workers it shows, so the wider acceptance changes nothing for it); `secrets_unavailable` without a directory. The not-shown case runs the same removal and answers `not_found` when it held nothing (no lookup on the hub goroutine). The removal runs off the hub goroutine under the store's lock with the workers' liveness read inside it (the janitor's review-S2 lesson; it decides whether an ended owner's directory still holds a file for someone), and the holders' counts are published before the ack. Audit: `AuditBegin` with the worker's id, `AuditEnd` with `{"removed": n}`: never a path's name or a byte. A hand-over not claimed yet is not the worker's: left alone. |
| 51 | A revoke racing an in-flight send | **The references in the text are checked last.** `Files.Revoke` records every path it removes (in memory, `RevokedFor` 24 hours) *before* unlinking any; `reviewHolds(rev, texts…)`, the check every route already makes last, right before a reviewed text's first byte goes (round 2 row 24's sites: `typeIn`, `prompt`, `terminalPrompt`, `promptViaServer`, the dialog's Other text, a dismissal's prompt, `answerAsync`, an agent handoff's request, a hire's prompt), now also refuses a text that refers to a revoked path: `secrets_review_stale` ("a protected file it refers to was revoked: review it again"), unsent, its command's files removed as for any failure before the send. **Reviewed or not** (fix round, reviews L3–L5): the switch's check needs a review (`rev` nil: none), the revoked-path check does not, so it runs for every send that carries references: with the switch off (a switch-off route changes only by this check), a schedule's stored prompt and a hire's successor (it holds files by a lease it never reviewed: `hireReviewHolds` at seen, before each Codex try and on the lane before the typed prompt; a refused hire prompt removes the files its own review made, as a switch change does, and a schedule's fire fails saying so), every text of a `worker.answer_ask` (all of them before the dialog's first key, each again right before it is typed: a revoke between two texts stops the dialog there, half answered and not submitted, where row 24's switch change does not, because after a switch change the references still name files and after a revoke they name nothing; the dismissal's prompt keeps the revoke's code instead of `prompt_failed`), an LLM handoff's instruction (before `Generate` and in its model-slot gate; not the reduced transcript: it is the worker's history, holding the references of every earlier prompt, and checking it would refuse every handoff of a worker for 24 hours after its revoke), a preview's text and `hire_preset.check`'s prompt (their model gates), and every pending sentence a `hire.interpret` follow-up sends the model (review R5P2-1: `preview.extra`, checked with the text by the same gates, the switch on or off; `reviewedSources` passes own references unreviewed and reads no source with the switch off). Every model payload's fields, checked or not: packup.detect's classifier and extraction read only the text (a suffix of it, image markers masked); hire.interpret's `command`, `pending_hire` and `hire_options` (the catalog: no references); hire_preset.check's `prompt`; an LLM handoff's instruction, its facts (the bridge's and git's: names, checkout, branch, status lines, skills) and the transcript (history, above); the transcript-reading calls (follow-up detection, activity classification, digest summaries) are history too. So no reference goes to a file revoked before that check; a send whose check came first went, and the revoke then removes the file. A file a command writes after the revoke is new and its worker's (it goes with the command's failure, stays with its success): never a file without an owner. The identical retry after a revoke writes new files (its reuse entries are dropped). A revoked path named again within 24 hours is refused the same way (it would name nothing). Rejected: a per-worker revoke generation captured at the gate and plumbed down every send path to the same checks (one more value through a dozen signatures to answer the question the text itself answers, with spurious refusals of files written after the revoke); serializing the revoke on the worker's input lane (a wrap-up's, an agent handoff's and a hire's files are written off the lane, and a revoke would wait behind a prompt waiting for its agent); rotating the reviewer (every open review in every tab would go stale). |
| 52 | `Worker.secret_files` | The store counts them (`SecretFileCounts`: files of the worker's own directories ∪ files it holds by a lease, distinct); `secretfiles.Options.Changed` is called after every operation that can change a holding (write, remove, claim, lease, release, expiry, revoke, sweep) and wakes one coalescing goroutine that reads the counts and, on the hub goroutine, sets each changed worker's field and emits its `worker.upsert` (`syncFloorWorkers` keeps it). A revoke reads and publishes them itself before its ack. Each change is numbered once made, and counts read after an older change than those published are dropped, so a recount that read before a revoke never lands after it. A pending owner's files count for nobody until claimed; an ended owner's directory kept for a holder counts for the holder. `omitempty`: snapshots and fixtures without files are unchanged. |
| 53 | Leases | **A holder row per file** (`prompt_secret_lease (dir, name, worker_id)`, cascading with its file), not a copy and not a row per owner directory: a directory holds every file of its worker, and a lease of it would keep files the handoff never named. A file lives while its owner holds (a live worker, a pending owner not expired) or any holder is live. `Release` (a worker's end, a failed request's pending owner), `ReleaseExpired` and `Sweep` take the workers' liveness and read it with the files locked: an ended owner's files a live worker holds stay (the directory and its row stay for them), the rest go; a holder's end lets its leases go and removes a file nobody else holds; the janitor forgets the leases of a worker that is not live (it ended while the bridge was down, or its release failed). `Revoke` removes a file for every holder. Rejected: promoting a holder to owner when the owner ends (per-file leases may have different holders in one directory: no single new owner; renaming files to move them would break every reference). |
| 54 | Which files a handoff names, and who its successor is | **Recorded at filing, held at hire.** When a handoff is filed (literal: its text; agent: the document the agent wrote and the request's protected instruction; LLM: the document and the job's instruction), `noteHandoffSecrets` records the bridge's own references in those texts that name files still there (`prompt_secret_handoff (handoff_id, dir, name)`, cascading with the handoff and the file; opaque names only). The successor is a worker **hired** (`worker.hire`, `run.start`, a schedule's fire) whose first prompt names the handoff's path (the cabinet's Hire from handoff and a schedule's `handoff_path` compose `handoff.HireTask`) or names files by their references; the path is matched as the store has it (`HandoffSecretsIn`: a filed path the text holds, whole, not inside a longer path nor running on into a longer name; fix round, review L2: splitting the text at blanks cut a directory with a blank, which `handoff.New` allows): `leaseSuccessor` lets it hold them once herdr shows it, right after its own files are claimed (the same moment, for the same reason: row 17), with the switch on or off (the lifecycle runs either way). A file named directly is held by whoever names it in a hire's prompt: a path is 130 bits of `crypto/rand`, so naming one means having been given it (a sent prompt, a handoff), and holding only keeps a file longer, never shows it (row 59: the files are no access control). Only a hire is a successor: a `worker.prompt` to an existing worker holds nothing new (the brief's successor; a consumer that exists already has its own run). A file that went before the successor was seen is not held: a handoff "send home" ends its worker at once, and its files go with it unless a successor already holds them. Rejected: a pending lease on the cabinet's document until someone is hired from it (a handoff lives for days: the files would outlive every agent run, as row 19 refuses for stored prompts); counting the instruction alone (the instruction is part of the handoff's text the brief names, and the document may not repeat it). |
| 55 | Native child agents | Subagents inside the worker's own session (#22, #23 child rows) share its files and lifetime: the registry's rows, removals and a replaced session's generation are keyed by `ch_…` ids and agent sessions, never by a worker id the file store knows; `liveWorkers`, `releaseSecrets` and `Revoke` see worker ids only, and nothing in the children's code calls them. Proven end to end: a child running and shut down, a second child dropped with a replaced session, the janitor sweeping meanwhile: the worker's file stays; the worker's end removes it. |
| 56 | Reconnect, resume, crash and restart | Kept (tested): floor sleep and wake, a herdr session gone and back, a bridge restart with the worker open in the store (the janitor counts store-open workers live), a reboot that herdr restores the workers from **when the directory survived it** (a `--secrets-dir` on disk is the restart case). The default directory is a tmpfs (row 7: never a disk-backed fallback): a reboot empties it, the startup sweep forgets the rows, the counts go and the next review writes again. Removed (tested): a worker the store has closed whose release never ran, a lease of a worker the store does not know, an expired pending owner, a row without a file, a file without a row, and an ended owner's file once its last holder closed too. **A workspace that closed while the bridge was down** (fix round, review L1) was never seen to close (the bridge closes a worker only when it watched its floor run without a gap), so it stays open in the store, and worker tracking keeps it so (its name held, its history): only the files' liveness reconciles. `liveWorkers` reads the open workers with their session and workspace, and `secretsLive` (on the hub goroutine, inside the files' lock as every liveness read) counts an open worker the hub does not show as ended for its files once **its floor has run without it for the grace**, each condition for a case that must keep them: its session's real floor is in the hub and running (an asleep floor's workers are shown; a gone session's come back: `removeFloor` drops the floor), its last observation was a running one with workers (`sessionState.looked`: not before the bridge has seen the floor run, so the startup sweep keeps everything, and not on a `KeepWorkers` observation that could not look), it is not a hire or a send home in flight there, no hire there is creating a workspace (`syncWorkers` holds new workspaces back meanwhile), and its stored workspace is not in the raw observation (a main checkout kept from the workers). The grace is one `SecretsSweep` by the bridge's clock from the first liveness read that found it so (any read: a sweep, a release, a revoke), cleared whenever a read finds it shown or not eligible: a floor whose workspaces show a little late (herdr restoring them) keeps them, a worker back keeps them. At the default sweep they go 5 to 15 minutes after the floor's first running observation; its leases go with it (`heldFiles` forgets a holder that is not live). The same rule covers a gap in the watch while the bridge runs (a reconnect's fresh observation without the worker). Until they go, a revoke removes them (row 50). Rejected: closing absent workers in the store at the first observation (it would change #2's worker tracking, names and history for every feature, and one observation is not proof); a grace counted in observations (herdr sends one per change, so two can come within a millisecond while it restores). |
| 57 | `worker.wrapup` with a hand-over (orchestrator addition, 2026-10-18) | `secrets_pending` (packup.detect's, for the same worker), checked as `worker.prompt`'s (`pendingFor` when the command comes: expired, another worker's, the switch changed, unknown are `secrets_review_stale`). A prompt that is exactly a text the hand-over answered as reviewed, or that text, `"\n\n"` and more, needs no review for that text (the longest such text); **the rest is scanned alone**, and its `secrets` is the review of the rest alone (its own scan and offsets, as round 2's per-text reviews are), so the game reviews only what the user added (the cleanup sentence). Any other prompt is reviewed whole. In the arming goroutine, after the gate and the limits and before the arm, the hand-over's files are claimed by the worker (`claimPending`, revalidated); a failure removes what the gate made; an arming that fails after the claim leaves the claimed files with the worker (as `worker.prompt`'s). The audit row says `secrets_pending: true`, never the token. |
| 58 | `World.prompt_secrets.dir` (orchestrator addition, 2026-10-18) | The absolute directory, present only while `available`, in the snapshot, `prompt_secrets.get`/`set` and `prompt_secrets.update`: a client tells the bridge's own references (`<dir>/<owner>/<file>`, both names `[A-Z2-7]{26,64}`) from look-alikes exactly, as `Files.IsFilePath` does. It is a path of the bridge host, no secret. |

## 2026-10-19 — #26 (phase 5 of #20): a child's own conversation, live, from the board

A child row on the floor overview seats you at its worker and opens **that child's** conversation over the worker's:
live while it runs, its history once it is done, with the way back. Code: `TranscriptChild` and `availability` in
`internal/proto/transcript.go`, `Registry.Child`, the target-keyed watches and the child logs in
`internal/server/transcript.go` (`txKey`, `txChild`, `txKids`, `syncKidTranscripts`), the per-child taps in
`internal/usage/session.go` (`WantChildren`, `Child`, `SetChildTap`); in the game `TranscriptWatches` by target,
`ImageFeeds` by target, the child sub-state of `TranscriptMode`, `laptop/transcriptChild.ts` (the breadcrumb and the
words), `Laptops.openChild` and `App.goToWorker(…, child)`; the fixture bridge's `tools/fixture-children.ts` and child
watches in `tools/fixture-transcript.ts`. Docs: `protocol.md` "A child's transcript (#26)".

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The target | The worker's `id` plus an optional **`child: {id, generation, provider}`** on every transcript command and on `transcript.items` / `transcript.closed`. `id` is the registry **row id** (stable for the row's life, also when the native id arrives), `generation` the worker's `child_generation` the client saw. The bridge resolves the row with `Registry.Child(worker, row)` and the path from the row and the worker's own session, never from the client: a generation that is not the worker's now is `stale`, a row the worker does not have (another worker's, removed, merged) or of another provider `not_found`. Provider-neutral, so #27's shared-server children plug into the same target. |
| 2 | Who reads the child's file | **The worker's usage session, once per file** (`transcript.Log`'s rule): the tracker already tails every Claude `agent-*.jsonl` and, with a listener, every Codex child rollout; a watched child gets a **tap** on that tail (`usage.Session.SetChildTap`) and a `transcript.Follow` log from where the tail is (`Session.Child`: path, file identity, next offset, a Codex child's history start), as the worker's own transcript does. Not `transcript.Read` plus `Refresh` (the nested expander's `agentLogs`, kept for it) and not a second tail. A watched child's file not read yet is looked for in every poll (`WantChildren`), not every `SubagentRescan`; a Codex session with no listener reads only its watched children's rollouts. A child's taps are voided when its file goes (`ErrGone`: `not_found`) or every file is read again (a replacement: `resync`). |
| 3 | Two watches per seat | Watches are keyed by **target** on both sides (`txWatches.byC[c][txKey]`, `TranscriptWatches` by `targetKey`): the worker's own watch stays open under a child's, so its view (scroll, pages loaded) is the same one when you come back; its pushes keep feeding it while it is hidden. Each child watch has its own cursors and sequence (its file's) and its own `sent` hashes: an image sent on one watch is not one the other may read. |
| 4 | Bounds | **2 child watches per connection** (`MaxChildTranscriptWatches`), apart from `--max-transcript-watches`, so a child can never push a worker's watch out; a third evicts the oldest (`transcript.closed {evicted}`; a seat shows one child, the client unwatches before it watches another). **16 children's logs bridge-wide** (`MaxChildTranscriptLogs`; one child watched by two connections is one log): another past it is `capacity`. A log goes with its last watch, and a completed child watched again is read again from its file: its history stays discoverable. |
| 5 | Liveness | A child's log is the tracker's, offered to its watches each round like the worker's (`txOffer` by target, with the child's `avail`), and pushed through the same throttled `Subscribe` path: at most 4 pushes a second. A Codex child's log has `CodexHistoryStart`: its parent's copied history is hidden, never shown as the child's activity. |
| 6 | Missing logs | `availability` on a child watch's head: a provisional row (no native id) or a file not written or found yet is **`pending`**; a row whose evidence says `unavailable` (and no file) is **`unavailable`**; a file that is there is read whatever the row says. Never the parent's or a sibling's log. While pending a change comes as a head alone; once the file appears the same watch goes live (a push with the page and the head). A file that goes closes the watch `not_found`, and the client's re-watch acks `unavailable`. The view says each in words ("hasn't written anything yet", "has no conversation to show"), never an error code. |
| 7 | Staleness | The hub checks every child watch after each observation and each child evidence (`syncTranscriptWatches`): a new generation closes it `session_changed`, a row gone `not_found`. The client drops a push or ack of a child it no longer watches, or of another generation (`Watch.gen`, `ready`, and the child's generation); the seat also checks the store every frame. A replaced session (or a child gone) returns the view to the worker's with a note on the seat bar ("Nibble started a new session: its subagents went with the old one"). Two workers in one directory never cross: the path comes from each worker's own session (`TestChildTranscriptTwoWorkersOneDirectory`). |
| 8 | The view | A second render of the transcript view, **read only**: no prompt box (its place says "Subagents take no prompts here." with "Back to <worker>"), no cards, no context meter. Its bar's title is a **breadcrumb**: a back control with the worker's name, a chevron, the child's name (and type) and its state in the floor overview's own pip and words (`childSinceText`), so the row you clicked and the page you land on read as one. Older items come on request ("Show earlier messages", `transcript.page` with the child's cursor; the scroll stays put). The images tab and the terminal keep the child open underneath. |
| 9 | Esc | **Esc goes back to the worker's conversation first; the next Esc stands you up** (`docs/shortcuts.md`). The seat bar follows: its keys say "Esc Back to <worker>", its note "Reading <child>'s conversation", and the stand button stops naming Esc while a child is open. |
| 10 | Activation | `OverviewHost.goToChild(workerId, childId)` → `App.goToWorker(workerId, 'transcript', childId)`: the seat first (as before), then `Laptops.openChild` with the store's row. The wall stays draw-only. The nested `subagent` expander in a worker's timeline (`agent` on `transcript.page`/`item`/`image`) is unchanged. |
| 11 | Fixture bridge | With `sim=1`, a children fixture's recorded child events are the simulated world's children from the start (`tools/fixture-children.ts`; it plays no recorded events); `sim.child` / `sim.child_session` change them. Child watches answer as the bridge does (pending / unavailable from the row, a Codex child's own long timeline, eviction, `stale` / `not_found`), and `sim.transcript {child, head?}` pushes to one. |

Coverage:

| Bullet | Where |
|---|---|
| A running child streams; a completed one shows history, older pages and images | `TestChildTranscriptWatch`; `TestChildTranscriptBounds` (completed history); e2e `h26-child-transcripts` "a child row opens…" |
| Back to the parent, the parent unaffected | `TestChildTranscriptWatch` (the worker's watch pushes beside it); `transcriptMode.children.test.ts` "opens over the worker's…"; `transcript.integration.test.ts` "#26…"; e2e "…Esc goes back…" |
| Session replacement and two roots in one directory | `TestChildTranscriptWatch` (replaced: both close, `stale` after); `TestChildTranscriptTwoWorkersOneDirectory`; `transcriptWatches.test.ts` "a late ack or a stale push…"; e2e "…a replaced session returns to the worker" |
| Missing / pending log: an explicit state | `TestChildTranscriptPendingThenLive`; `transcriptMode.children.test.ts` "pending, then unavailable…"; e2e "a child with no transcript and one not written yet…" |
| Watch and cache limits with many children | `TestChildTranscriptBounds` (2 per connection with eviction, 16 logs, an evicted child read again) |
| Codex: inherited history is not the child's | `TestChildTranscriptCodex`; `usage` `TestChildTapCodex` |
| One reader per file | `usage` `TestChildTap` |

## 2026-10-19 — #27 (phase 6 of #20): Codex subagents through the shared app-server

A shared-server Codex worker's children, tracked live through the app-server that owns its conversation, on the
bridge's existing join of its thread, on the same rows as #25's rollout evidence, their transcripts through #26's
target. Verified on **codex-cli 0.160.1, 0.162.1 and 0.163.0**. Code: `internal/codexapp/children.go` (`Thread`'s child
metadata, `Spawn`, `AgentItem`, `ChildNote`, `ChildReader` and the `Watcher`'s reads, `Descendants`),
`internal/codexchild/server.go` (the `Source`'s server half: `Joined`, `Notify`, `Lost`, the observer, `combine`),
`CodexChildren` and `dropCodexWatch` in `internal/server/codexserver.go`, the forward in `codexNotification`, the wiring in
`internal/app/world.go`; the mock's collaboration directives in `internal/codexshare/mock.go`. Research:
`docs/research/codex-server-subagents.md`. Docs: `protocol.md` "Codex subagents through the shared app-server (#27)".

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | One source or two | **One `codexchild.Source`**: the server's word is kept beside the rollouts' facts in the same book and goes out through one derivation (`combine`) and one queue. Two `childagents.Source`s would each have their own emit goroutine, so after a restart the tracker's first read of a killed child's rollout (`running`, it has no end) could land after the server's recovery (`notLoaded`) and win. Not in the registry: #22's registry is provider-neutral and last-wins, and "authoritative while joined, not once the connection is lost, but its ends stay" needs per-session knowledge it does not have. Proven by `TestServerOverRolloutAfterRestart` (20 rounds). Evidence the server decided says `source: app_server`. |
| 2 | Which source's state wins | **The server, once a join of the session was seen this run** (`owned`); the rollouts give the rest (names, parent, transcript, times). Joined: `running` is the server's; the end of the latest turn it showed is the state; `idle` (loaded, no end seen) takes the rollouts' end when they have one, else is `idle`; `notLoaded` takes the rollouts' end, else `unknown`. Lost: an end stays (the server's or the rollouts'), anything else, the rollouts' `running` included, is `unknown`. A session never joined keeps #25's rule exactly (`TestNoJoinKeepsTheRolloutRule`). No flapping: one derivation decides, the rollouts never flip a server state back (`TestServerLiveOverRollout`). |
| 3 | `idle`, `completed`, `unknown` | **`completed` / `interrupted` are a turn's end** (the parent's `subAgentActivity` `completed` / `interrupted`, the child's own `turn/completed`, `failed` as `interrupted`), as #25 reads them, so a v2 child that finished its task reads `completed` from both sources, not `idle`. **`idle` is loaded with no end known** (Codex's status alone does not say how the last turn ended: `PendingInit`, `Completed` and `Interrupted` are all `idle`). **`unknown` is not in memory with no end known.** A child that goes `idle` with no end within `Settle` (1 s; the probe's order is idle, its turn, the parent's completed) gets its last turn read without items (`thread/turns/list`): its status is the end; in progress, none or refused (ephemeral) leaves it `idle`. An end shown before a lost join is read again at the next recovery (row 13). A fresh child's first `idle` (its pending init, before its `started`) shows nothing. `systemError` is read like `idle`. |
| 4 | Discovery | **The parent's items and broadcast statuses, and a recovery on every join**: `subAgentActivity` (`started`: dispatch id = the spawn call's id; v2 shows no `collabAgentToolCall` but `wait`) and v1's `collabAgentToolCall` receivers name children on the spawner's stream (a nested spawn is on its parent child's); a status, turn or close of a thread not known yet is read (`thread/read`, no turns) and is a child when it is spawned (`thread_spawn`) and its parent chain reaches the worker's thread; a thread that is not is remembered (1024). Each named child's metadata is read once. A recovery on every join (a connection made after a spawn is not subscribed to the child, and a rejoin's `thread/resume` returns no children): `thread/list {ancestorThreadId}` (experimental, negotiated: the watcher sends `experimentalApi`), whose rows carry the live status; refused (any JSON-RPC error: no capability, no state DB), the loaded threads read one by one plus the newest `sourceKinds: ["subAgentThreadSpawn"]` rows, both kept by parent chain (not by `sessionId`: a child's is its own id on 0.163.0). That fallback cannot see an unloaded historical child the list misses; the rollouts still show it. A known child the recovery does not list (ephemeral) is read; one not loaded is `notLoaded`. |
| 5 | Joining a child | **Never.** The parent's join already carries the child's events (connections initialized before a spawn are auto-subscribed), the broadcasts (`thread/status/changed`, `thread/closed`) and the parent's items cover a child spawned before the connection, and the settle read covers an end not on the parent's stream. A resume would emit `thread/goal/cleared` to every subscriber of the child, the terminal included, and one with an override can reload an idle child. So no child is resumed, loaded or given a turn, and no read carries an override: AC2 by construction (`TestChildReadsSendNoOverride`; the fixture counts no `thread/goal/cleared` of any child, no extra model request, unchanged model and effort). |
| 6 | Unsubscribing | **Only the bridge's own connection's, by leaving.** The watcher's leave is its `thread/unsubscribe` of the root and its connection's close, which drops every subscription that connection held, the auto-given child ones included (the server's `connection_closed`); `thread/unsubscribe` is per connection, so nothing of the terminal's is touched. No per-child unsubscribe: it would change nothing the close does not. A running child is never unloaded or stopped by it (`TestCodexShareChildrenNoExtraTurns`: three bridges left, the child then ended for the terminal). |
| 7 | Loss and recovery | **A loss drops every live claim; a join counts once recovered.** The hub calls `Lost` on the watcher's disconnect, failure and close, and at every site that drops a join (`dropCodexWatch`: the join's own close event is ignored once it is not the worker's). `Lost` and `Joined` forget the live claims (ends stay, unverified until the recovery reads them: row 13); a join is `attached` only after its recovery, and nothing of the session is sent while it recovers (`recovering`), so a bridge's join shows a running child `running` throughout (no `unknown` in between, `TestJoinDoesNotFlickerARunningChild`) and a rejoin after a SIGKILL never shows a stale `running` (`TestServerRejoinTrustsOnlyItsRecovery`, the fixture's state sequence `[running unknown]`). A failed recovery leaves the claims `unknown` and is tried again after 2 s. A queue past 1024 notifications is dropped for a new recovery. The server is never asked to replay; the reads are bounded (10 s each, 5 pages of 100, 64 loaded threads). |
| 8 | Ephemeral children | **Live only, defined apart from the root's refusal.** The root watcher still refuses an ephemeral root (`ErrEphemeral`); a child is ephemeral exactly when its spawner is (fixture, three versions), so a shared worker has none in practice, but one is handled: `transcript: unavailable` whatever else says (no rollout, ever: #26's view says it has no conversation), its state from the events, `idle` when its turns cannot be read, its end kept when it unloads or the bridge reconnects (it is never listed; read while loaded, else not in memory). Its row stays as long as the worker's generation (the parent's rollout still names it). |
| 9 | Transcripts | **#26's target, from the rollout.** A shared worker's usage session already reads its children's rollouts (#25), so a shared child's transcript opens through `TranscriptChild` with nothing new; `transcript` is the rollouts' (`pending` while the server names a child whose rollout is not read yet). Not `thread/read`: its turns are a different shape from the rollout parser's, hydrating them is deprecated on paginated threads, and a live child's rollout is there. |
| 10 | Root handling unchanged | `codexNotification` forwards every notification of the worker's current thread's join to the observer before its root filter; the filter and everything after it are unchanged, so a child's turn never touches the root's running turn, questions or sends. The observer keeps what names a child (items only when they mention `subAgentActivity` or `collabAgentToolCall`). |
| 11 | Experimental capability in tests | `codexapp.Options.StableAPI` initializes without `experimentalApi`: a test knob for the refused-filter path against the real server (production always negotiates it). |
| 12 | Fixture | The mock gains `MOCK:spawn`, `followup`, `message`, `interrupt`, `wait` (the v2 tools, in the `collaboration` namespace the request offers); a child's task arrives as an `agent_message` whose `encrypted_content` is the plain payload. Headless suites (a worker-style app-server, a driver in the terminal's place, the bridge's own pieces) cover the protocol; `TestCodexShareBridgeChildren` runs herdr-world with the real TUI. Versions: 0.160.1 and 0.163.0 through `VerifiedCodex`, 0.162.1 with a local, uncommitted entry (`VerifiedCodex` lists 0.162.0, not installed here); `VerifiedCodex` and `SupportedLines` unchanged. |
| 13 | Review round 1: an end missed while the join was lost (R1) | An end the bridge showed (`completed` at 2000) stayed across a loss and beat everything after the rejoin: the recovery only took the listed status (`idle`), never read the turn, and the end came before the rollouts in `combine`. A follow-up that ran and was interrupted (or completed after an interrupted one) while no join saw it left the old state and time on the row indefinitely. **An end carried over a loss is unverified until the next join's recovery reads that child's last turn** (`thread/turns/list`, one turn, no items), once, before the join's claims stand (still `recovering`, so nothing half-read is sent), and only when the recovery does not find it running (`active` ends it already). The end knows its turn: the parent's `subagent-completed-<turn id>`, the child's own `turn/completed`, a settle read. The same turn, none, or a refusal (ephemeral, a legacy child not loaded) keeps the end as it was, time included; a newer turn that ended is the end at its `completedAt` (whole seconds; the real server gives it on 0.160.1 and 0.163.0); one still in progress supersedes it (the rollouts' end, else `idle` or `unknown`). An end not tied to a turn (`interrupt_agent`'s, a v1 close) is kept when the turn read ended the same way (or any way, before a close) no later than a second after it. Bound: one read per child whose end this bridge showed, per join; never a read for a child it did not see end, so a historical child still costs nothing (row 7). Rejected: a newer rollout end superseding a server end in `combine` (the times are in different units, `0` after a settle read, and it would let the rollouts flip a live state, `TestServerLiveOverRollout`); dropping ends at a loss (an ephemeral child has no rollout to fall back to). The registry keeps a row's last `ended_at` when a superseded end leaves it `unknown` or `idle` (only a run clears it, #22). Tests: `TestServerReconnectMatrix` ({none, completed, interrupted named and not} × {nothing, follow-up completed, interrupted, running, server restarted, unreadable}), `TestServerReconnectOverRollout` (the rollouts', a killed follow-up, a bridge restart: no read), `TestServerMissedFollowupEnd` (the reviewer's), `TestServerLossAndRecovery` (a read only for the child with an end); fixture `TestCodexShareChildrenMissedEnds` (both directions on the real server). |

Known bounds, not fixed: a session's book with server facts is never evicted (one per shared root session the bridge
joined this run); a child thread's server request (an approval inside a child) is recorded in the root join's open
requests, and its `serverRequest/resolved` (the child's thread id) is dropped by the root filter, as before #27.

Coverage:

| Bullet | Where |
|---|---|
| Spawn, interact (message), follow-up, wait, interrupt, close resolve to the correct child; tool-call status never the child's | `TestServerLifecycle`, `TestServerV1CollabCalls` (close, a wait naming the child), `TestCodexShareChildren` (real Codex: spawn with its dispatch id, a timed-out wait, follow-up, message, `interrupt_agent`), `TestCodexServerChildrenEndToEnd` (hub) |
| Loaded, unloaded and ephemeral children | `TestServerLossAndRecovery` (loaded running and idle, a restarted server's `notLoaded`), `TestServerEphemeralChild`, `TestServerIdleReadsTheLastTurn`; fixture `TestCodexShareChildrenServerLoss`, `TestCodexShareChildrenEphemeral` |
| Nested children attach to their recorded parent; two concurrent stay distinct | `TestServerConcurrentAndNested` (a grandchild found by its status, its spawn on its parent's stream later, a guardian and a foreign thread no rows); `TestCodexShareChildren` (`alpha` and `beta` at once, `inner` under `alpha`) |
| Historical reads start no turn and change no setting | `TestChildReadsSendNoOverride` (every request's fields), `TestCodexShareChildrenNoExtraTurns` (three joins and recoveries: no model request, no turn, model and effort unchanged, no `thread/goal/cleared`), `TestServerLossAndRecovery` (a recovery reads the last turn only of a child whose end it showed before the loss) |
