## 2026-10-19 — #116: direnv is a mise shim with no version selected

A Codex hire with the shared-server switch on fell back to Codex's built-in server with mise's whole multi-line diagnostic
as its note (`direnv status: direnv: exit status 1: mise ERROR No version is set for shim: direnv …`), shown as it was on
the seat bar and in the hire's toast. The investigation (`docs/research/codex-direnv-preflight.md`): the bridge's PATH is
shim-first, direnv is installed but no version is selected for the worker's directory, so the shim passes `exec.LookPath`
and then fails. The fallback itself stays (#18, #155, #186). Code: `ExecError`, `DirenvUnselectedError` and the
recognition in `Preflight.Check` (`internal/codexapp/preflight.go`), the Warn in `hireShared`
(`internal/server/codexserver.go`), `codexNotice` (`game/src/world/codexServer.ts`), the fixture's `simfail=codex_direnv`
(`game/tools/fixture-codex-server.ts`).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Missing, or present and unusable | **Not the same.** A direnv that is genuinely absent is still skipped (nothing to check). A shim that exists but cannot run is a refusal: the `.envrc` could not be validated, so it is neither "direnv missing" nor "no `.envrc`". Any other nonzero exit stays the generic `direnv status: …` refusal. |
| 2 | Recognition | The runner's failure is a typed `*ExecError{Name, Err, Stderr}` (its text exactly as before, `Unwrap` to the exec error, stderr kept to 4 KiB instead of 300 bytes). `Check` turns an `ExecError` whose stderr carries mise's `No version is set for shim: direnv` (or `mise which`'s `is not currently active`) into `*DirenvUnselectedError{Dir, Detail}`. Matching the text is the only signal mise gives: its exit code is 1 like any failure. |
| 3 | One line out, the detail kept | `Error()` is `direnv is installed through mise but has no version selected for <dir>`: that is the persisted note (`shared Codex server: …; started the usual way`) and the hire result. `Detail` is mise's stderr; `hireShared` logs it at Warn with the worker and the directory. The wake path runs no preflight (`startSharedServer` only), so it has no such note. |
| 4 | Laptop copy | `codexNotice` recognizes that one line (the same words on both sides, pinned by a test in each language) and says what it is, where to fix it (`docs/git-worktrees.md`) and what the worker is left with, and to send it home and hire a new one. No mise lines. Other reasons render as before. |
| 5 | Remedy | Documentation only (`docs/git-worktrees.md`): the bridge's environment and the worker's pane both need a selected direnv; per-worktree `mise.local.toml`, a bridge `Environment=MISE_DIRENV_VERSION=…`, or a global `mise use -g` as the host owner's choice. **The app never runs `mise use`, installs, trusts a config, writes `direnv.toml` or runs `direnv allow`**, and does not choose a version for the host. Rejected: probing `mise which` to pick a binary path (it would make the app choose a version policy, and a stale path breaks on upgrade). |
| 6 | An existing fallback hire | Persisted as `legacy`; it is never migrated, by a fix or by toggling the setting. Send it home and hire a new one (documented). |
| 7 | Tests | Through the real `ExecRunner` with executable `direnv` scripts in `t.TempDir()` (`TestPreflightRealRunner`: inactive shim, `mise which` wording, other failure, no `.envrc`, allowed, blocked, denied, missing executable; `TestExecError`); `TestSharedCodexHireDirenvUnselected` (the exact note, the legacy launch, the usual start, the Warn); `ui/codexServerSection.dom.test.ts`, `ui/hiredToast.test.ts`, the fixture test and `e2e/h155-codex-server.spec.ts` (`simfail=codex_direnv`). |

## 2026-10-19 — #66 (part 5 of #61): schedule suggestions from agent replies

When an agent's final reply says a step has to wait ("24h soak, until about 10:45 UTC tomorrow; after the soak: delete
the backups"), the bridge drafts the schedule and the reply offers it as a chip beside Handoff. **Nothing is scheduled
without a save in the form.** Code: `internal/schedsuggest` (the gate question, the extraction's request and
validation, the settings `Service`), `internal/server/schedsuggest.go` (the hub's part, on #90's turn end in
`internal/server/followup.go`), `internal/store/schedsuggest.go`, `internal/proto/schedsuggest.go`,
`transcript.Turn.Message`, `followup.Service.Scored`; the game's `world/scheduleSuggest.ts`, `ui/scheduleSuggestionsSection.ts`,
the chip in `laptop/transcriptRender.ts`, `ScheduleFormPrefill.dueAt` in `ui/scheduleForm.ts`, `App.openFollowup` /
`sendZone`; the fixture's `tools/fixture-schedsuggest.ts`. Tests: `go test ./internal/schedsuggest`,
`go test ./internal/store -run ScheduleSuggest`, `go test ./internal/transcript -run FollowupTurnMessage`,
`go test ./internal/server -run 'ScheduleSuggest'`, `world/scheduleSuggest.test.ts`, `world/scheduleTime.test.ts`,
`laptop/transcriptSuggestion.dom.test.ts`, `ui/scheduleSuggestionsSection.dom.test.ts`, `ui/scheduleForm.dom.test.ts`,
`tools/fixture-schedsuggest.test.ts`, `e2e/schedules.spec.ts`.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Package and hook | `internal/schedsuggest`, modelled on `internal/followup` (a `Service` with settings, `View`, the env override and the threshold's bounds; `Roles`; a `Store` interface), importing only `internal/ai` (`TestScheduleSuggestUsesOnlyAIInterfaces`). The hub reuses the follow-up questions' trigger: the same `followupUpdate` from the same `FollowupTracker`, the same 2 s settle (turn ended and herdr not `working`), the same skips (an ask, a blocked worker, a freelancer, not Claude or Codex, an empty message), the same message and `{"last_agent_message": …}` state, the same turn hash. No second tracker: `considerFollowup` looks at a settled turn for each feature that is `ready` and has not seen the message, and `runTurn` runs them. |
| 2 | Classifier calls | Both features to look at the message → **one `ClassifyMany`** with both gate questions (`followup`, `schedule`), one slot and one retry. Follow-up questions alone → their own `Classify` through `followup.Service.Detect`, unchanged (every #90 test is untouched and green with suggestions off, the default). Suggestions alone → one `Classify` with their question. The same `ai.Service` roles (`ScheduleSuggestRoles` defaults to `FollowupRoles`, then `AI`), so the slots, timeouts and the retry are the shared ones. |
| 3 | No starvation | With both, the follow-up extraction runs **first** and its result goes to the hub before the schedule extraction starts (`TestScheduleSuggestionNeverDelaysFollowups` holds the schedule's LLM call and sees the follow-up shown meanwhile; `TestScheduleSuggestionBothOneClassifyMany` checks the order of the LLM calls). The turn stays pending until both results came (`followupCand.left`), so each judges staleness against the same turn; a failed, timed-out or stuck schedule step never touches the follow-up. |
| 4 | Gate | "Does the message say that a step must be done later, after a waiting period or at a specific future time?", default threshold 0.7, bounds 0.05–0.99 (the follow-up questions'). |
| 5 | Extraction | One LLM call in JSON mode, temperature 0, no partial answer, its own 45 s timeout, no retry of a call that may have reached the provider; cut off or empty, once more with effort `none` / `minimal` when the model's catalog takes it (#60's rules). It gets the message's last 96,000 characters, the current time in UTC (with the weekday) and the user's zone with its local time and offset, or "not known: read clock times without a zone as UTC". It answers `{"due_at","title","draft_prompt"}` or `{"none":true}`; the system prompt says the draft addresses a fresh agent, describes the deferred steps with the message's names and ids, and says the original message is attached as a handoff to read first. |
| 6 | Validation | Any of these is **no suggestion, recorded as seen**: `due_at` not RFC 3339 or without an offset / `Z`: `time.Parse(time.RFC3339)` refuses both, and the exact shape is checked too, because Go's parser also takes a one-digit hour, a `,` fraction and offsets like `+24:00` or `+01:60` (which shift the instant silently): two-digit fields, a `.` fraction of any length, an offset hour ≤ 23 and minute ≤ 59, upper-case `T` and `Z` only (Go refuses the lower-case ones RFC 3339 allows; the request asks for "an explicit offset or Z"); at or before now (the clock **when the answer came**, `TestValidatedAtAnswer`); more than 30 days after it; an empty title or prompt; a prompt over 32 KiB or starting with `--`; unparseable JSON; a cut-off answer (`ai.KindTruncated`); a timeout or any other failed call. `due_at` is kept in UTC. The **title is clipped** (folded to one line, control characters out, 200 bytes with `…`: `proto.ScheduleMaxTitle`); the **prompt is rejected, never clipped** (a cut prompt would lose steps; tabs become four spaces and other control characters go, so Claude's typed check passes). `TestScheduleSuggestBounds` keeps the package's bounds equal to `proto.ScheduleMaxTitle` and `herdr.MaxPrompt`. A classifier failure is not recorded (a later look may try again), as for the follow-up questions. |
| 7 | Time zone | A bridge-wide stored preference (`schedsuggest_settings.zone`), last writer wins. The game sends its zone (Settings → Day and night's, else the browser's) with **`schedule_suggestions.zone`** on connect (after the snapshot, once the connection is live) and when that setting changes, only when it differs from the stored one, and **never in answer to an update** (two browsers in two zones would send theirs back and forth). The bridge accepts an IANA name Go's `time.LoadLocation` loads, not `Local`, not an offset. Unset → UTC, and the request says so. The chip shows the time on the **viewing** browser's clock (the form's zone, `browserZone()`, so the chip and the prefilled form agree) with UTC beside it; the stored zone only feeds the extraction. |
| 8 | Delivery | `Worker.schedule_suggestion {id, message, due_at, title, draft_prompt, score, at}` in the snapshot and the worker's upserts. `id` is the turn's id (`transcript.Turn.ID`), what dismiss names; `message` is the reply's message id, Claude's `message.id` or Codex's message item id (`transcript.Turn.Message`, new, equal to the handoff candidate's `message`, `TestFollowupTurnMessageIsTheCandidates`), so the chip lands on the candidate's row. It lives until accepted, dismissed, or the transcript goes on: a new prompt or turn (`moved`). **A turn is its `id`**, not its message's hash: a newer turn whose reply repeats the older one's word for word closes it too (`moved`; the tracker can read the prompt and the reply in one poll, with no prompt in between to close it), and a result is current only for the worker's latest turn's `id`, so a result that comes back after the turn was superseded, by a turn with the same reply included, is recorded and never shown (`TestScheduleSuggestionStaleResult`, `TestScheduleSuggestionRepeatedWhileInFlight`). Follow-ups clear by hash (#90, unchanged); here the chip must name the current reply's row, and a retained suggestion of an older one would stay open on the bridge, invisible in the game. Unlike a follow-up, herdr saying `working` alone does not close it (the transcript's next prompt does). An open one survives a restart, restored only onto its own turn: when the latest turn is a newer one with the same reply (written while the bridge was down), the record closes as `moved` instead (`TestScheduleSuggestionSameTextNewTurn`). |
| 9 | Dedup and closing | Its own table, `schedsuggest_seen` (worker, SHA-256, the suggestion as JSON, `outcome`: `accepted`, `dismissed`, `moved`, `stale`, `gone`; the last 20 per worker), not a column on `followup_seen`: the two features look at a message independently (one may be off, or switched on later), and each must know only whether **it** looked. A closed suggestion keeps its first outcome and never comes back, after a restart or a re-read either. **The hash stays the dedup key**: each (worker, SHA) is looked at once, in flight included (the hub keeps the set of hashes whose extraction runs per worker, each cleared when its result comes; A, then B, then A again while A runs makes two looks). So a newer turn with an identical reply gets **no suggestion of its own**: the older one closes (`moved`, row 8) and the message was looked at; should its look still run, its result is stale (recorded, not shown). Asking again for the same text would cost the same calls for the same answer, which the user has just seen or let go. |
| 10 | Accept = save | Opening the form from the chip changes nothing on the bridge. A `schedule.create` whose `source` is `{kind: "suggestion", worker, message}` with the worker's open suggestion's `message` closes it (`accepted`, after the schedule is stored); a create from the plain "Schedule follow-up…" (`kind: transcript`) or another message leaves it. Cancelling the form leaves the chip. |
| 11 | The chip | On the candidate's row, **in place of** "Schedule follow-up…", beside Handoff: one button "Schedule follow-up · tomorrow 12:45 (10:45 UTC)" (the existing clock icon, not an emoji; the day in words on the viewer's calendar: today, tomorrow, the weekday within the week, else the date) joined to a × ("Dismiss the suggested follow-up", a button of its own, after the chip in Tab order) that sends **`worker.dismiss_schedule_suggestion {id, suggestion}`**. The chip is the plain button's family, filled (the agent proposes a time) with the time in tabular figures. Its click opens the form prefilled with the title, the exact `due_at` (kept to the millisecond until the field is edited, like an edit's), the draft prompt, the source worker's harness, model, effort and folder, "Attach this message as a handoff" on, source `suggestion`. **A time that passed while it showed** keeps the chip and says so ("suggested today 12:00, passed"); the form opens with that time in the field, flagged "The suggested time has passed: type or pick a new one.", and Save waits for a new one: the work still has to be done, and the draft prompt is worth keeping. A minute tick keeps the day words and the passed state true while the chip shows. |
| 12 | Setting | "Schedule suggestions" in Settings → AI, after the follow-up questions (section id `schedule-suggestions`): off by default, the threshold, the privacy note above the switch, the zone the bridge reads times in, `--schedule-suggestions-enabled` / `HERDR_WORLD_SCHEDULE_SUGGESTIONS_ENABLED` (read-only in the panel, `env_locked`). Needs both roles: while one is not ready the state is `incomplete` with `missing`, the switch says which model and its state ("Unavailable until both models are ready (LLM: not set up)…") and links to the AI integration. **No test gate**: the follow-up questions' test exists because a positive gate flags a worker as needing you; here a positive gate shows a chip that schedules nothing, and every invalid answer is already no suggestion, so a test would cost a click and an inference for little; `schedule_suggestions.set {enabled: true}` needs only both roles ready (`incomplete` otherwise). The AI integration's "used by" lists name it for both roles. |
| 13 | Fixture | `tools/fixture-schedsuggest.ts`: `simschedsuggest=on|off|incomplete|env|env-off|none` fixes the setting's state with no models (without it, the simulated AI integration's rules); `simsuggest=<key>` starts Zippy with the rollout reply and its suggestion, a dismissed or saved one remembered by the key across a reload (which plays the reply again without it); `sim.suggest` gives any worker one. Dismiss, a save from it, `worker.prompt`, `sim.prompt_turn` and `sim.final` clear it as the bridge does (`tools/fixture-schedsuggest.test.ts`). |

Coverage:

| Bullet | Where |
|---|---|
| Golden cases (deterministic): rollout summary, "in 2 hours", "after the 24h soak", next steps with no time, a past time, a follow-up question only, a Codex `last_agent_message` | `TestGolden` over `internal/schedsuggest/testdata/golden.json` (messages in `testdata/messages`, the Codex one a real-shaped rollout read through `FollowupTracker`) |
| Golden cases (live, gated like `followup/live_test.go`) | `TestLiveGolden` (skipped unless `H3D_SCHEDSUGGEST_LIVE` names the bridge's `ai.json`; each case's UTC `due_at` within its tolerance, or none) |
| Gate below / at / above the threshold | `TestGateThreshold`, `TestScored`; `TestGolden` (gate cases make no LLM call) |
| Extraction none / invalid / truncated / timeout | `TestParse` (malformed RFC 3339 included: `+24:00`, `+01:60`, a one-digit hour, a `,` fraction, lower-case `t`/`z`), `TestParsePromptText`, `TestExtractFailures`, `TestValidatedAtAnswer`; on the bridge `TestScheduleSuggestionNeverDelaysFollowups` (a timeout: no suggestion, follow-up kept) |
| Dedup: same SHA once; restart → no call, open one restored | `TestScheduleSuggestionRepeatedWhileInFlight` (in flight), `TestScheduleSuggestionSameTextNewTurn` (a newer turn with the same reply: no call, none of its own; after a restart not restored onto it), `TestScheduleSuggestionDismissAndRestart`, `TestScheduleSuggestionNeverDelaysFollowups` (after a restart), `TestScheduleSuggestionAcceptedBySave`, `TestScheduleSuggestSettingsAndSeen` |
| Setting off sends nothing; a missing role runs nothing, state incomplete | `TestNotReadySendsNothing`, `TestScheduleSuggestionNotReadyMakesNoCall` |
| Both on → exactly one `ClassifyMany`; follow-ups-only unchanged | `TestScheduleSuggestionBothOneClassifyMany`, `TestScheduleSuggestionOffLeavesFollowups`, every `TestFollowup*` untouched |
| Follow-up extraction not delayed by the schedule step | `TestScheduleSuggestionNeverDelaysFollowups`, `TestScheduleSuggestionBothOneClassifyMany` (call order) |
| Accepting never schedules without a save | `TestScheduleSuggestionAcceptedBySave` (no schedule before `schedule.create`; a transcript create and another message's leave it; the matching one closes it, across a restart); `transcriptSuggestion.dom.test.ts` (the click only hands it to the host, the chip stays); `scheduleForm.dom.test.ts` "from a schedule suggestion" (prefill, Save sends `source: suggestion`, Cancel sends nothing); `e2e/schedules.spec.ts` (chip → form → Save → schedule, chip gone) |
| Dismissing persists | `TestScheduleSuggestionDismissAndRestart` (stale and unknown ids refused, closed across a restart); `transcriptSuggestion.dom.test.ts` (×, a refused dismiss keeps it; the keyboard lands on the plain button that returns); `e2e/schedules.spec.ts` (× → gone, a reload keeps it gone) |
| The transcript going on clears it | `TestScheduleSuggestionTranscriptMovesOn`, `TestScheduleSuggestionSameTextNewTurn` (a newer turn with the same reply), `TestScheduleSuggestionStaleResult` |
| The setting: off by default, env/flag override, threshold, unavailable per missing role | `TestSettings`, `TestZone` (package); `TestScheduleSuggestionsSettings` (bridge: set, zone, update events, `env_locked`, `incomplete`); `ui/scheduleSuggestionsSection.dom.test.ts` |
| The chip's text, row and time | `transcriptSuggestion.dom.test.ts`, `world/scheduleSuggest.test.ts`, `world/scheduleTime.test.ts` (`dayClockText` across a date boundary) |
| Turn message = handoff candidate's message | `TestFollowupTurnMessageIsTheCandidates` |
| Docs | `docs/protocol.md` "Schedule suggestions", `docs/architecture.md` "Schedule suggestions" and "AI roles and their callers", this entry, CONTRIBUTING's package list and flag table |

## 2026-10-19 — #117: the plain Hire worker's "Add herdr hiring instructions", and a question at Hire

A plain Hire worker whose first task starts other agents ("let's start an agent for each service") put them in split panes
and on its session's real floor, the problem #95 fixed for presets; the workaround was to save the task as a preset, tick
the box and hire from that. The plain form now has the box, and Hire asks when the classifier says the task starts agents
and the box is off. This reverses #95 decision 4 ("Plain Hire worker … have no box") and decision 7 ("never on Use or Hire")
for the plain worker form only. Game only: `worker.hire`, `hire.prepare` and `hire_preset.check` are as #95 made them.
Code: `ui/hire.ts` (`instructionLines`, `instructionsControl`, `hire`, `askWanted`, `delegates`, `ask`), `ui/hire.css`;
`world/hirePresets.ts` (`nudgeWanted`, `instructionsBlocker`) as the preset editor uses them. Tests: `ui/hire.preset.dom.test.ts`,
`ui/hire.ask.dom.test.ts` (its `hire_preset.check` is the fixture's own gate), `ui/hireCoordinator.test.ts`, `e2e/h117-plain-hire-instructions.spec.ts`, `internal/server/hirepresetcheck_hidden_test.go` (the bridge takes the redacted text).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The box | Every Hire worker form on a bridge that adds the lines (`hirePresets.instructions`, as #95 decision 6: an older bridge shows nothing and nothing sends the flag) has the box, **off** by default, with "What's added", the byte count and the 32 KiB blocker exactly as the form from a preset has them. The hint is its own wording on a plain form ("Tick it if this task starts other agents…" off, "Each agent this worker starts…" on); "for this hire only; the preset has it…" is only for a preset's form. Save as preset… carries the box over (it already sent `instructionLines() !== null && addLines`). |
| 2 | The question | At Hire, with the box off, the first task gets `hire_preset.check` (same wire command, unchanged: no rename, no bridge change) when `nudgeWanted` says so: the bridge has the box and the check, the classifier is `ready`, no `h3d_floor` in the task, and the player did not answer "Hire without" for exactly this text. A "yes" asks **in the dialog** by the buttons (#95 decision 7's callout, not a second modal): **Hire with instructions** / **Hire without**. A form from a preset never asks: its box is the player's own choice (the preset editor already asked at Save, and "Save as is" is its answer). |
| 3 | After the secrets review | The check runs after the review of #108, on the review's resolved text; the prompt is never logged (`net/redact.ts` already covers `hire_preset.check`). `hire_preset.check` is a stored-prompt review on the bridge (#108 round 2: it takes a review that leaves every candidate as typed and refuses one that protects anything, `secrets_review_stored`, before it classifies), so the review is sent only when it protects nothing: then the text and its `secrets`, as the preset editor's `delegates()`. A review that protects something is not sent and is never rewritten as "keep as typed" (the classifier would read the value the player chose to protect): the check carries the text with **every marked range**, protected or left as typed, replaced by `[redacted]`, and no `secrets`. The bridge scans that text and finds nothing (`[redacted]` is no value to it, in an assignment too; `[secret]`, which the composers draw, is), so it classifies it as a plain prompt. The hire itself still carries the review and the typed text (`classifierView` in `ui/secretsFlow.ts` is for the check only). If the bridge still refuses the check (a value the redaction left a candidate in), it hires as typed with no question. Only a "yes" in time stops the hire: a timeout (the client's 1.5 s), an error, `unknown_command`, a classifier that is not ready and a "no" hire as typed, with no question. |
| 4 | The answers | **Hire with instructions** ticks the box and hires with the flag; **Hire without** hires as typed and the game remembers it per desk's draft for the page's lifetime (a failed hire and Hire again does not ask twice; another text asks). **Esc** goes back to the form without hiring and keeps the task (the dialog does not close). Editing the form (the task, a pick, the box, the desk) takes the question back, so an answer never hires something other than what was asked. |
| 5 | Enter | The footer says "Enter hires", so the Enter that pressed Hire must not answer. The question is built only after the classifier's answer, focus moves to it then, and a repeating key (Enter held down since Hire) is refused on its buttons: only a fresh press answers. Hire again while it is open only refocuses it. |
| 6 | Size | `added` and the image budget are computed before the review with the box as it was. "Hire with instructions" rechecks the limit with the lines (`instructionsBlocker`, on the resolved text when a review made one, whose image paths the form's text does not have); over it, the form comes back with the box ticked and the blocker shown, nobody hired. Otherwise `added`, the flag and the budget the coordinator resolves against are the ones with the lines, so the payload is consistent with the box. |
| 7 | Background hiring | The check and the question come before the dialog closes, as the secrets review does (#210): at most 1.5 s, only when the gate is on. Skipping the question for a background hire would miss the case this ticket is about. Esc or Close during the check hires nobody ("Not hired: it was closed before its first task was checked."). |
| 8 | Not changed | The dictated hire review (`ui/hireReview.ts`) never sends the flag, scheduled hires never add the lines, and Hire orchestrator's `runPrompt` always does: follow-ups if wanted. |

## 2026-10-19 — #119: the overview's now line loads as a split-flap board, and lines arrive without moving the board

While AI summaries were written, the floor overview's "Working on" column jumped: rows grew as a fallback gave way to a
two-line model line, the metadata after a line changed width and moved the cut of the text beside it, and a new now
line flipped in with nothing to say it was coming; a model line's refresh had no signal at all (#198 left `pending` out
beside a model's line). Code: `workerDigest` (`internal/server/digest.go`), `statusOf`, `line()` and `titleKey`
(`game/src/world/overview.ts`), `lineStatusText` (`world/digestSettings.ts`), the kept column and now line
(`ui/overview.ts`: `what`, `nowLine`, `place`), the clock (`ui/flaps.ts`), `overview.css`, the fixture's pending
(`tools/fixture-digest.ts`).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A refresh of a model's now line | **Reverses #198's "never `pending` there".** The bridge sends `now_status: {state: "pending"}` with `now_source: "llm"` only while that worker's now-line call is in flight; newer steps that wait for their gap or settle, or for the daily cap, stay silent beside a model's line (a wait is not a call in progress). The status is part of the composed digest, so the hub publishes a `worker.upsert` when the call goes and another when it lands: one more per call, already rate-limited. A model's task line still has no status. |
| 2 | First summary over a fallback | **The skeleton covers the fallback** (the user's call): a fallback now line (title, recap) with `pending` and no `reason: daily_cap` shows the flap cells instead of its text. Under the daily cap, retrying, failed, or the feature off, the fallback shows with its words as before. A pending now line with no fallback text at all is kept as an empty line (`line()` no longer drops it) and shows the same skeleton; under the cap it reads `No summary yet` with `AI waiting`. |
| 3 | The task line | A fallback task line with `pending` keeps its text (it is stable) and shows the busy mark in its slot instead of `AI pending`. Only the now line gets the skeleton. |
| 4 | Refresh on the page | The model's line stays readable, a step back through its own colour (`--ov-text-refresh`, never an opacity: 0.66 over an asleep row's dimmer tokens fell to 3.23:1), with the busy mark where its age was. Each is ≥ 4.5:1 on the ink and the hover row and dimmer than the settled line: Quiet `#8a95b4` (asleep `#7d89ab`), Ubuntu `--text-3` (asleep `#b896ae`: the UI has no tone under `--text-3`); never a skeleton over a readable line. `lineStatusText(pending, kept)` has no chip, so the lounge wall (out of scope, `render/overviewScreen.ts`) shows the age alone as before. |
| 5 | The rebuild trap | Each worker row keeps its "Working on" column and its now line element across refreshes: `fill()` builds the rest of the row again (an activity tick changes `rowSig`) and `place()` puts the kept column back without moving it; inside, the ticket and task line are rebuilt only when their own signature changed, the now line is updated in place from what it shows. Motion is driven by the line's text and state changing, never by the row's signature. |
| 6 | Layout | The now line takes two lines' height (`min-height: 38px; 2lh`), the task line one, `No summary yet` two. The metadata slot is always there (empty too), at least 14ch wide (11ch for a now line on a phone, 3ch for a task line), right-aligned, with a zero-width space for a baseline, and the text before it takes the line's room: the slot sits at the line's end, so its states line up down the board and never move the text. **This moves the age and words from right after the text (#232) to the line's end.** **The label keeps the sparkle's room only while its line awaits the model's** (the user's call): the skeleton, and a fallback now or task line with `pending` (any reason, `daily_cap` too, so a capped wait turning into a call does not shift it) get the same sparkle, hidden and `aria-hidden`, so the text keeps its left edge and width through pending → skeleton → arrival, a pending task fallback → the model's task, and a refresh → the new line. A settled fallback (no status, retrying, failed, the feature off) has no room: **#232's "no width kept for a sparkle a line does not have" stands for settled lines**. Always reserving was tried in review round 2 and left a 16 px gap after every fallback's label. The residual: a call that lands within one page refresh (4×/s) of starting goes from a settled fallback to the model's line with no pending shown, and its text shifts once, by the sparkle's room. A failure's chip with Retry (up to ~30ch) is not reserved: it grows the slot, and on a phone goes under the line as before (#174). No `contain` or `content-visibility`. |
| 7 | Glyphs | The board's capitals and figures (`A–Z0–9`) in the data font, on tiles drawn like the header's counts. `░▒▓█` were tried first and read as a hatched stripe at a line's size. Never braille (neither the Quiet data font nor H3D Box has it). The busy mark is CSS-drawn: two small flaps whose upper leaves turn. |
| 8 | Arrival | A model's line resolves left to right: each letter is a cell holding its own (unseen) character, so it keeps that character's width in the proportional face and the line never reflows, with a flap glyph drawn over it from `data-g` (`content: attr(data-g) / ''`, nothing for a screen reader); at the end the text is one text node again. 140 ms lead plus a 280 ms sweep, lines that arrive together 60 ms apart (at most 3 steps): none over 600 ms. One shared rAF clock (`FlapClock`). Other now lines (a recap, a title) keep `ov-flip-in`. Kerning and ligatures are off on the now text so cells and text measure the same. |
| 9 | Calm | `data-calm` stops CSS animations only; the clock asks `calm()` itself: no job runs, a resolve shows its text at once, and turning calm ends a running one. The skeleton is a still bar in the flap colours saying `summarizing…`; the busy mark stands still. |
| 10 | Accessibility | `aria-busy="true"` on a loading now line, its cells in an `aria-hidden` wrapper, the row's label `Now: AI summary loading`, then the text once it arrived (`; refreshing` beside a model's line whose refresh is out). No live region. |
| 11 | Titles that tick | Default Claude and Codex titles do not change per tick once herdr strips the leading glyph, but Codex can put a spinner later in the title or blink `[ ! ]`/`[ . ] Action Required`. A title's now line is compared through `titleKey` (braille U+2800–28FF and the action marker removed, spaces collapsed): no flip when only those changed. |
| 12 | Tests | Go: `TestDigestNowPendingBesideModelLineOnlyWhileCalling` (pending and its two upserts, none during the gap or settle, failed and retrying after); `TestDigestNowFailedRefreshKeepsLineWithStatus` now expects pending while its refresh is out. Game: `ui/flaps.dom.test.ts`, `ui/overview.flaps.dom.test.ts` (skeleton, arrival, activity ticks during both, refresh, `titleKey` flips, calm, the task line), `world/overview.test.ts`, `world/digestSettings.test.ts`, the wall's `lineMark`, `tools/fixture-digest.test.ts`; `e2e/m119-flaps.spec.ts` reads every row's box and Turnip's lines, text slots (left edge and width) and metadata slots before and after loading → arrival → refresh → the next line (a pending prompt's task becoming the model's at the same step; desktop and phone), composes the refreshing text's contrast in the browser for every row state in Quiet and Ubuntu, and checks reduced motion; `ui/overview.flaps.dom.test.ts` checks where the label keeps the room (skeleton, pending and capped fallbacks: yes; settled, retrying, failed fallbacks and the model's lines: no); `render/overviewScreen.test.ts` checks the refresh tokens (Quiet) and that no refreshing rule has an opacity or filter. `e2e/h232-overview-activity.spec.ts`'s quiet waiting chip is Sprout's daily-cap wait (`AI waiting`): a line only pending shows the skeleton now. |

## 2026-10-19 — H3D-2: the model and effort of a worker nobody hired through the bridge

Workers a hired coordinator started with a raw `herdr agent start … -- -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=medium` showed the OpenAI icon and an **empty** model line (#229): their workspaces had `h3d_floor` and no `h3d_harness` / `h3d_model` / `h3d_effort`, and only a bridge hire has a record. Their Codex rollout said `gpt-6.1-sol` / `medium` all along (and `usage.model` already carried the model). The bridge now recovers it; the game is unchanged, every surface (both overview surfaces, the HUD, the prompt, the laptop, handoffs) reads the same `worker.model` / `worker.effort`. Code: `Hub.shownModel`, `setUsage`, `syncFloorWorkers` (`internal/server/hub.go`, `usage.go`); `usage.CleanModel` / `CleanEffort` and the Codex and Claude readers' `Effort` (`internal/usage`); `agentLine` (`internal/server/runprompt.go`). Tests: `internal/server/modelmeta_test.go`, `modelmeta_internal_test.go`, `internal/usage/observed_test.go` (fixture `testdata/codex-turn-context.jsonl`), the hiring-instruction pins (`runprompt_test.go`, `hireinstructions_test.go`, the game's `fixture-start`, `e2e/m6-start.spec.ts`).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Where | **In the hub, not in `modelText`.** The bridge sends the effective `model` / `effort` in `proto.Worker`, so no consumer needs a fallback and the game gets no `usage.model` fallback. |
| 2 | Precedence | **Per field** (model and effort alone): **1.** what the transcript of the worker's *current* agent session says; **2.** what was reported: the hire op, the stored record, the `h3d_*` tokens (today's behaviour, remembered across herdr restarts); **3.** unknown (empty). **Never the floor's hire defaults.** Observed wins because the ticket wants the *actual* model, and a direct hire that switches model mid-session must show the switch. A direct hire declared `X high` whose transcript says `X high` shows no change (no upsert flips the label); `Y medium` shows `Y medium`; no transcript shows `X high`. |
| 3 | Kept apart | Observed values are the worker's `usage.model` / `usage.effort` (additive `effort`, #101's rule), kept with the transcript session they were read from (`Hub.usage`, `usageFor`); the reported ones in `Hub.reported`, which is what `metaOf(prev)` reads (not the view, which may hold the observed ones) and what `persist` stores. **Observed values are never stored**, never become the hire record, and a bridge restart reads the transcript again. "Preserve direct Hire worker metadata": the hire's values stay in storage and are the fallback, never overwritten by what a transcript said. |
| 4 | Lifetime | The observed value follows the **latest** `turn_context` (Codex) or main-thread assistant line (Claude): a model or effort change shows. It is dropped as soon as the worker's agent session changes (`shownModel` compares the transcript session the usage was read from, the rollout a cwd lookup found included, with the worker's now, and the tracker clears the usage on its next round; a usage found by cwd before herdr named a Codex session stays while herdr names none or names that same rollout, and goes with the first upsert that carries another session), then re-derived from the new session's transcript; until that says anything the reported values show. A worker whose usage is gone loses it with it. Completed and idle workers still on the floor keep showing it. A transcript that appears later (the tracker looks again every 30 s for one it missed) is shown when it does. |
| 5 | Events | `worker.usage` carries no worker fields, so a usage that changes the shown model or effort goes out as a `worker.upsert` (which carries the usage); one that does not stays a `worker.usage`. |
| 6 | Codex evidence | The latest `turn_context`'s top-level `effort`, else `collaboration_mode.settings.reasoning_effort`; the model as before. A turn that states no effort leaves it unknown (the reported one shows), never the previous turn's. |
| 7 | Claude evidence | Model: the last assistant message of the main thread, a sidechain's line in the main file not counted (`Usage.Model`; the reader's own `model`, which also sets the context window, pricing and cache evidence, still follows the file's last line, as ever). **Effort: read from the top-level `effort` field of main-thread assistant lines**, found by reading `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` on this host: all 40,734 main-thread assistant lines of every session there (Claude Code 2.1.300–2.1.303) carry it (`high`, `xhigh`, `medium`, same values as `perTurnEffort` and as `api-request.params.output_config.effort`), and for all 60 stored Claude hires with an effort the last line's `effort` equalled the hire's. The orchestrator's `api-request-blob` `message.output_config.effort` is on a few hundred records only and is not used. Claude Code does not document the field: the latest main-thread line decides, so one without it, or with a value that is not a plain level name, leaves the effort unknown (the reported one shows) even when an earlier one had it, and a sidechain line never moves it, set or clear; nothing is guessed. A renamed field costs the observed effort only. |
| 8 | Normalising | An observed model id is shown as the hire catalog launches it: Claude's `[1m]` mark dropped (the catalog's id pattern cannot hold it, so a direct hire's transcript names the model its record does and the label does not flicker), `<synthetic>`, empty, overlong and unprintable ids are no evidence. An effort must be 1–16 lower case letters (the launch rule). An alias a hire stored that the transcript resolves (`opus` → `claude-opus-5-5`) is the observed model's, by row 2. |
| 9 | Hiring instructions | `hireInstructions` (#95, #117) asks one more thing, `agentLine`: tag every workspace with `h3d_harness`, `h3d_model` and `h3d_effort`, what the agent is started with, in the same `report-metadata` call as the floor token, because the floor shows them as that agent's model line. They are the reported fallback (a coordinator that follows them shows its worker's model before its transcript says it, and after a restart); the transcript is what wins. Run prompts, `hire.prepare` and `worker.hire` with `herdr_instructions` all carry the line. |
| 10 | Protocol | `usage.effort` is additive (absent from older bridges and when a transcript records none); `worker.model` / `effort` keep their wire shape and change meaning only as row 2 says. See protocol.md ("What `model` and `effort` show", "Usage and cost"). |

## 2026-10-19 — H3D-1 (Kaneo): Telegram's "Questions only" mode, and episodes named by their question

Telegram sent too much to be read: 228 `needs_you` messages in three days, about 6% answered. Most were orchestrators
over the review-pass cap and freelancers' report requests re-alerting each time their status flipped (the episode was
`status_since`), bare blocked statuses with no question, and a generic alert before each question's cards. Code:
`internal/notify/questions.go` (the identity, the mode's text), `service.go` (`Settings.Mode`, `sight`, `alert`,
`admits`, `deliver`, `sendAudit`), `buttons.go` (`openCards`' ring and row, `openMenu`, `carded`), `tracker.go`
(`Alert.Key`, `reopen`), `rule.go` (`Report.Request`, `WrapUpArmedAt`), `internal/server/notify.go` (`reportRequest`),
`internal/store/notify.go` (`migrationNotifyMode`), `internal/proto/notify.go`; the game's `world/notifySettings.ts`,
`ui/telegramSection.ts`, `tools/fixture-telegram.ts`.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The setting | **A mode, `everything` or `questions`** (`Settings.Mode`, `notify_settings.mode TEXT DEFAULT 'everything'`, `notify.set {"mode"}`, `NotifyState.mode`): a string, not a flag, so a selector reads as one. `everything` is the default and today's behaviour; a row saved before it reads `everything` (the migration's default), and the game reads a state without it (an older bridge) as `everything` too. Another value is `bad_request`. It refines the needs-you event: `events.needs_you` off sends nothing in either mode. |
| 2 | The selector | Settings → Telegram, between the switch and the events: **What to send**, a native radio group (`Everything that needs you`, `Questions only`), each described. Under Questions only the finished-work switches (`A worker finishes`, freelancers) stay where they are, greyed out, described by "Questions only: finished work is never sent."; their positions are kept for when the mode goes back. The privacy note says the question's text goes with Questions only too. |
| 3 | What qualifies (Questions only) | A valid `ask`, a valid `followup`, a valid permission or folder-trust menu (`validMenu`), a freelancer's report request **whose `input_required` the message shows** (scrubbed, non-blank). Not: done, a wrap-up `needs_you`, an orchestrator over its cap, a bare `blocked`, a report request with no text. The report qualifies (not zero messages) because its request is a question in the worker's words and showing it answers the ticket; `input_for` (orchestrator or user) is not checked, as the inbox does not check it. |
| 4 | One message per question | The question is the message. Replies on and cards it can have (an ask, a follow-up of 1–4 questions, a menu): **its cards alone**, no alert; the first card rings unless `quiet`, the rest are silent (#14's `c.Quiet = true` now holds only when an alert rang first). Else **its text** (`questionText`): the questions and options, a menu's ask, what it is about and its choices, a report's request (1500 runes), then "Replies are off: answer in the game." (or that a reply is typed into the worker, when replies are on). A secret ask's text is only "A question waits in the game (its answer is secret).". Filtering stays apart from Allow replies. The broader mode's messages are unchanged. |
| 5 | Menus without the alert | Under Questions only the blocked status is an episode that may not notify (known silently), and the menu read later is an episode of its own (`menu|<operation>`), so its sighting opens the card: through `rang` and `openMenu`, as #88, with the spell from that sighting. Every menu card of the mode rings (`openMenu` asks the mode), and one more operation in the same spell is one more ringing card. A spell that never shows a menu sends nothing. Review R1/R2 (round 2): the menu episode is `menu|<decision>|<native>`: `Menu.Decision` is `opOf`'s key without the blocked spell (`op.key` folds `since` in for #106's cards, so the same permission seen in another spell was a new episode and rang again), set by `menuFacts`; the native call is the one the decision was first seen with, held by the loop (`menuEpisode`, next to the tracker): a call known later is adopted (one prompt rings once), another call is a new decision (#106 row 4) in every form, the replies-off text too. `Op`, `Hash` and `Native` keep their card and answer roles. A menu episode that notified, seen again in another spell (a working spell between ends its card, #106), sends nothing new and gets its card back, silent (`rang` with no ring), if that spell has none. A screen-only menu asked again identically after it was answered is the same decision (nothing tells them apart; with a native call known, the new call is new): with replies off under Questions only it sends nothing, with replies on its card comes back silent. Review N1 (round 3): the loop holds each worker's decisions, not only its last menu's (`menuEps`: worker → decision → native call and id), each while the tracker holds its episode (known, shown or current: `tracker.holds`, so the bound is the tracker's), so a decision first seen without a native call, adopted one, then seen again after other menus keeps its id and sends nothing; another known call under it is still a new decision. In the broader mode a bare block's menu stays inside its blocked spell's episode (a second alert when the menu is read would break #88); a worker whose needs-you is not its blocked status (a report request, a cap, a wrap-up) gets its menu as an episode of its own in either mode, an alert and its card as before, since its later blocked spells are no longer new episodes (found in the final check: `TestMenuOfAWorkerWithARequest`). Switching modes inside a spell can send that one question once more. |
| 6 | Episode identity, every mode | `episode()` names a needs-you episode by what it is about, not when the status changed: an ask `ask|<tool_use_id>`, a follow-up `followup|<turn_id>`, a report request `report|<sha256 of its trimmed input_required>`, a wrap-up `wrapup|<armed_at>`, an orchestrator over its cap `crew|<pass>`, a bare blocked status `blocked|<status_since>` (a new spell is a new block), done `done|<status_since>` as before. The tracker knows each worker's latest 16 episodes, not its last one only, so a question seen again after another (a request after its worker's permission menu) is not new; review R5 (round 2): and every episode the worker still shows (`live`: its ask, follow-up, report request, stuck wrap-up, cap, menu), never evicted: the 16 bound only the others, so a request shown under many menus is still known; a report seen resolved forgets its request (`reopen`), so the same words asked again notify. As before, a working spell between does not make the same question new. `Judge`'s `since` and reason are untouched, so the shared vectors and the game's inbox (still `reason|since`) are too. `Alert.Key` carries the episode; `current` and `release` compare it. |
| 7 | One choke point | `admits(a)`: allowed (on, ready, its event; done never under Questions only) and, under Questions only, a question. `sight` (eligible), the settle (`due`), `release` and every `deliver` attempt check it, so an alert parked or queued before the mode changed is dropped (`TestQuestionsOnlyDropsWaitingAlerts`). Review R3/R4 (round 2): `form(a)` decides a question's form from the settings as they are (`Alert.Asks`: it is a question whatever the mode; `Question`, `Ring`, `Body` follow), and every place one waited forms it again: `alert`, `release`, each `deliver` attempt, a Ring card set's job and its release (`rings`). Switched off, needs-you off or the channel not ready, nothing goes, and `openCards` checks again before each card, after its pace. Replies or the mode changed, a text or alert in the sender, or a card set on the replier, is handed back to the loop (`handBack`, drained in `process` if its episode is still on, else dropped with `notify.send` code `obsolete`, as `deliver` does) and goes as the settings say now: replies off, its text (a secret ask's: only that one waits); replies on, its ringing cards; the broader mode, its alert and quiet cards. Never dropped for that. `TestWaitingQuestionMatrix`. Review R3/R4 (round 3): round 2 checked before the destination's pace, which can wait a minute or a rate limit's pause; now the decision is made at the last moment, after every wait, right before each send: `goes(a)` (form, `admits`, the form unchanged) in `deliver` after `lim.wait` on every attempt (the queue, the pace, a retry's backoff), and `cardGoes` inside each card's paced `call` (its pace, its rate-limit retry, between the cards of a set). A pace token taken for a call so decided against is given back (`limiter.refund`: no call was made), so the question in its new form does not wait one more pace. Only the tracker's own alert is handed back (`Alert.tracked`, set in `sight`, carried by `rang`, `openMenu`, a parked set of the same question): a menu card the replier opens of itself (`seen`: a replaced native call) that can no longer be cards is dropped, and its episode's alert, queued right after it, is formed again, so one question is handed back once, not twice (`TestReplacedMenuFormedAgainOnce`). The partial set: once a Ring set's first card went, the question went (it rang), so the set is not formed again: switched off (or needs-you off, the channel not ready), the rest is not sent and the sent cards end "answer in the game"; replies off, the sent cards end as replies off and the rest goes back as one text (`Alert.From`: the questions from there on, numbered in the whole set, always text whatever the mode, and quiet: the set rang already), nothing sent twice; the mode changed, the rest goes on, quiet as it was. Cards after a broader mode's alert (not Ring) only stop, replies off or switched off: the alert was the message. `TestSendTimeMatrix` (budget park, cooldown park, paced text, paced cards, between cards, retry backoff, a card's rate-limit retry × off, needs-you off, everything→questions, questions→everything, replies off, replies on). |
| 8 | Budget | A question going as its cards never takes the per-worker alert minute: cards draw on the card budget (3 sets per worker a minute, the destination's 10 a minute), as a cooldown-held alert's cards already did (#106 row 8). A text question is an alert and keeps every limit. |
| 9 | Audit | `notify.send` gains `reason`, `about` (`ask`, `followup`, `menu`, `report`, `wrapup`, `review_cap`, `blocked`, `done`: the reason alone cannot tell a bare block, a menu and a capped orchestrator apart), `via` (`cards`: the cards were the message, written by `openCards` with their count and no attempts; `question`: the text was) and `cards`. On an alert, `cards` is written once its cards had their turn on the replier (the row moved there from the sender): the cards of its question open then; a menu read after it is counted on its `notify.menu` row instead, never by waiting for it. A question's cards handed back (round 2) write `notify.limit` outcome `returned`; its text or alert then writes its own `notify.send`. A Ring set stopped part way (round 3) writes `via` `cards` with the cards sent; the rest's text its own row (`via` `question`). |
| 10 | Tests | Go (`newRig`, FakeChannel, FakeClock; `questions_test.go`): `TestReportRequestOnceAcrossStatusFlips` (the ticket's repro: `status_since` 60000/120000/180000, one message in either mode, under Questions only the request's text), `TestReviewCapOnceAcrossStatusFlips`, `TestWrapUpOnceAcrossStatusFlips`, `TestReportRequestResolvedThenAskedAgain`, `TestQuestionsOnlyAskCards` (single and multi-question, first rings, rows), `TestQuestionsOnlyFollowupCards`, `TestQuestionsOnlyMenuCard` (bare block nothing, the menu one ringing card), `TestQuestionsOnlySuppresses`, `TestQuestionsOnlyQuiet`, `TestQuestionsOnlyRepliesOffText` (text, secret, menu), `TestSendAuditReasonAndCards`, `TestModeSetting`, `TestQuestionsOnlyDropsWaitingAlerts`, `TestMenuOfAWorkerWithARequest`, `TestTrackerKnowsRecentEpisodes`; round 2 (review R1–R5): the reviewer's repros `TestMenuEpisodeAcrossStatusFlips` (server, the real codex-approval screen), `TestNativeReplacementRepliesOff`, `TestParkedQuestionAfterDisabled`, `TestParkedQuestionRepliesTurnedOff`, `TestUnresolvedReportAfterManyMenus`; `TestEpisodeMatrix` (ask, follow-up, report, wrap-up, cap, bare block, done, menu, a request's menu × both modes × replies: a line, a status flip, a working spell between, a new question, a replaced native call), `TestWaitingQuestionMatrix` (a parked card set, a parked alert, an alert between attempts × off, needs-you off, the mode, replies off, replies on), `TestTrackerKeepsLiveEpisodes`, `TestMenuCardBackAfterStatusFlip`; round 3 (review R3, R4, N1): the reviewer's repros `TestPacedSettings`, `TestNativeAdoptionAcrossInterveningMenu`, and `TestSendTimeMatrix`, `TestReplacedMenuFormedAgainOnce`, `TestMenuDecisionSequence` (adoption, replacement, menus between); store `TestNotifySettingsMode` (a pre-change row); server `TestNotifyCommands` (mode) and `TestNotifyFactsReportAndWrapUp`. Game: `world/notifySettings.test.ts`, `ui/telegramSection.dom.test.ts` ("what to send"), `e2e/h11-telegram.spec.ts` (the keyboard journey's new stop, and the mode with mouse, arrows and a phone). |

## 2026-10-20 — #125: compact transcript screenshot previews, kept on disk

Screenshot-heavy transcripts were slow to open and scroll. The investigation (docs/research/transcript-screenshot-compression.md)
measured the previews of one real workload at 4,030,365 bytes, 87% of them PNG previews at Go's `BestSpeed`, and every
preview cut again after a restart or the memory bound. Code: `internal/imgcache/imgcache.go` (`MakeThumb`, the
policy constants, `Cache.Thumb`, the derived disk layer), the bench in `docs/research/transcript-screenshot-bench/`
(`thumbs.go`, `app.mjs`, `browser.mjs`) and `make screenshot-bench`.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Codec | **Pure Go, no new dependency** (the user, 2026-10-20): imgcache keeps its "pure Go, no cgo" contract. WebP would save more (80.0% against JPEG's 75.0% on the same pixels) but Go has no WebP encoder; AVIF is a follow-up. |
| 2 | The policy (`MakeThumb`) | A JPEG source stays **JPEG q82**, byte for byte as before. A PNG, GIF or WebP whose preview is **opaque** is **JPEG q82, unless its lossless PNG is at most 2.00× the JPEG's bytes**: then PNG (flat interface and text screenshots, where JPEG saves little and blurs edges). A preview **with transparency** stays lossless PNG, never put on white. Kept PNGs use the default compression level (some 6% smaller than `BestSpeed` for about 4 ms more, paid once now that the preview is on disk). The PNG is encoded after the JPEG into a writer that gives up once it passes the 2× budget, so a photograph's PNG costs a fraction of a full encode. Go's `image/jpeg` writes 4:2:0 chroma only, so small coloured text on dark backgrounds is the readability risk: **the user reviewed every corpus preview side by side (420 and 240 px, DPR 1 and 2, 100% crops of the busiest region) and approved the policy as is on 2026-10-20.** |
| 3 | The threshold, measured | The 20 PNG previews of the sample are 4.75× to 9.04× their JPEG (median 6.72×): screenshots cut down to 480 px have tens of thousands of colours. So the sample cannot place the threshold: at any k up to 4 nothing is kept as PNG and the reduction is 74.89%; k = 5 keeps 2 (68.41%, under the 70% target), k = 6 keeps 6 (52.95%). 2× was chosen on principle (exact pixels when they cost at most twice the bytes), and the synthetic tests (`TestThumbCodecPolicy`: a flat interface screenshot at and above 480 px, a flat GIF) are what exercise it. |
| 4 | Bytes, measured | **4,030,365 → 1,012,160 bytes, 74.89% fewer** over the 40 previews (the 20 PNG previews 3,524,188 → 505,983; the 20 JPEG previews unchanged: the 10 with originals in the sample regenerate byte-identical). These are encoded bytes on the wire (base64 adds a third). They are not a saving in decoded bitmap memory, which depends on the pixels (the same 480 px), and not a promise of a proportional frame-rate gain. |
| 5 | Derived previews on disk | Under the image cache directory, apart from the content-addressed originals (a preview does not hash to its source's name, and `diskGet` would remove it): **`t/<variant>/<source hash>`**, `<variant>` = `v<thumbVersion>-<ThumbSide>px-q<quality>-png<keep %>-z<PNG level>` (now `v1-480px-q82-png200-z0`). `thumbVersion` is bumped when the code changes the output another way. On first use every other entry of `t/` (older versions, other settings) is removed, and leftovers in the current one. Each file is a 46-byte header (magic, format, mime, width, height, sha256 over the source hash, the variant and the preview) and the preview; a file that fails the check (damaged, truncated, another hash's, another variant's) is a miss: removed and cut again. Written as a `.tmp-*` then renamed, files 0600 in 0700 directories. `t/` is made on the first write, so a cache that never cut a preview looks as before; the originals' counting and trimming see only top-level files and never touch it. |
| 6 | Bounds | The derived previews have **their own bound, 64 MiB** (`MaxThumbDisk`, `Config.MaxThumbDiskBytes`), least recently used out first (a read refreshes the mtime), under their own mutex with the originals' discipline; the originals keep their 512 MiB. 64 MiB holds some 2,500 previews at the sample's average of 25 kB (a kept PNG can be 150 kB). Conversion stays at two at a time (`decodeSlots`), the memory LRU at 64 MiB shared with the originals. |
| 7 | `Cache.Thumb`'s order | Memory, then (inside the per-hash wait, so N callers for one hash make one disk read or one cut) the derived file, **before a decode slot is taken and before the original is loaded**, then the original (memory, disk, `load`) and a cut. A memory-only cache (`--image-cache -`) works as before. Errors are unchanged (a source that cannot be cut writes nothing), so missing, invalid and oversized images give the same protocol codes. Hash admission (`readImage`'s `wasSent`) and the protocol are untouched. |
| 8 | Callers | Every `MakeThumb` caller gets the policy: `Log.Thumb` (also without a cache), activity images, and Drop Zone thumbnails over HTTP (`Content-Type` is the preview's own mime). The game takes `ack.mime` (`toBlob`), `createImageBitmap` for prints and monitors, `<img>` for drop thumbnails, so a JPEG preview of a PNG works everywhere; the lightbox and downloads fetch the full original with its own mime (copy converts to PNG as before). |
| 9 | Measurement | A repeatable scenario the user reruns on their laptop before merging: **`make screenshot-bench CORPUS=<private capture>`** (builds the game, takes the e2e lock, leases a port; `app.mjs`): the built game with its 3D scene, seated at a worker whose transcript is the captured one, `transcript.image` served by a real `imgcache.Cache` (`thumbs.go serve`; `-legacy` is the code before), cold / restart / memory bridge × cold / warm page, both policies, three runs; it prints a summary table and writes the raw results into the corpus directory, nothing into the repo. On this host (NVIDIA RTX 2060 through ANGLE/Vulkan): after a **restart** 11 of 40 thumbnails used to show late (p95 433 ms), now none (the bridge answers in 0.21 ms instead of 162 ms); a **cold** bridge is conversion-bound either way (conversion 155 → 161 ms median: the bottleneck did not move into generation); frame gaps stay at one frame at p95, and the worst gap on a warm bridge went from 117 to 17 ms. `Timeline.regroup` takes 2–4 ms per whole session (open, a 12,000 px scroll, six live updates), so it was not changed. The isolated probe (`browser.mjs`) and the Go timings (`thumbs.go`) are extended with the policy. Numbers: docs/research/transcript-screenshot-compression.md, "Implementation results". |
| 10 | Tests | `internal/imgcache`: `TestThumbCodecPolicy` (photo-like opaque → JPEG, flat interface at and above 480 px and a flat GIF → PNG with exact pixels, translucent → PNG with its alpha, JPEG → JPEG), `TestThumbsSurviveARestart` (a new `Cache` on the directory: no `load`, no cut, the same bytes; 0700/0600), `TestStaleThumbVariantsAreRemoved`, `TestDamagedThumbFileIsCutAgain` (flipped byte, truncated, header only, empty, another hash's file, the original itself), `TestThumbDiskIsBounded` (LRU by read, the originals untouched), `TestConcurrentThumbsReadTheDiskOnce` (8 callers: one cut, then one disk read), `TestThumbFailuresAndMemoryOnly` (garbage, a header over the pixel bound, a failing `load`: the same errors, nothing written; no directory: memory only), `TestThumbDirIsNeverFollowed` (a symlinked `t/` is removed, its target untouched). `internal/server`: the cache's tree is 0700 directories and 0600 files with thumbnails under `t/`, a drop thumbnail's `Content-Type` is its bytes' type. |

## 2026-10-20 — The hire review's task is the shared composer

"Hire from handoff" (#223) and a dictated hire (#212) open the hire review, whose task was a plain textarea: no pasted
images, no `/` skills, no `@` files or `@r:` repositories, where every other prompt box has them. Code: `ui/hireReview.ts`
(`promptText` now exported from `ui/hire.ts`).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The box | **The shared composer** (#51), mounted once for the review as the textarea was, `#review-task` kept on its editor; the completion is the hire dialog's (#39): a `CompletionScope` over `hireSources`, its context the review's floor, harness and the folder and worktree `worker.hire` would get, none before `hire.prepare` answered and a harness is chosen. Supersedes #212 row 5's "no images". |
| 2 | Keys | `mod-enter` with no submit: Enter adds a line as before, and no key hires (#212 row 8). |
| 3 | The task's text | `ReviewChoice.task` is the composer's text as the hire dialog's form sees it (`promptText`: each image a bare `[Image #n]`, each file chip its `@` mention). Only a change of that text is an edit (`editTask`): an upload finishing, or a draft shown on open, leaves the origin (Dictated, From handoff) alone. An interpretation that replaces an unedited task shows it in a new draft. |
| 4 | On Hire | The draft is resolved first (the images uploaded, their paths in the text), before the secrets review and before the coordinator, which still gets no draft (`prompt: null`, #33). The review is busy meanwhile; a failed upload leaves it ready with the hire dialog's message and each image's Retry; Esc then says it was closed before its images were uploaded. The interpreter's hand-over still covers only the task exactly as answered. |
| 5 | Given back | A background hire's `Reviewed` keeps the draft, images too; a draft is disposed only when no hire on its way and no held review has it. |
| 6 | Secret references | Unchanged: a reference stays plain text in the composer (#108 row 48: no composer segment), and the line under the box names its files. |

## 2026-10-20 — #127: a schedule's "Add herdr hiring instructions", and a question at Save

A scheduled worker that starts or recreates other workers left them on its session's real floor: on 2026-10-20 a rollout
schedule hired its coordinator on the Monitoring virtual floor, and the coordinator recreated a worker's workspace to
resume its Codex conversation; the new workspace had no floor tag and showed on the default floor. Resuming a
conversation restores no placement. Nothing had told the coordinator what #95's lines tell a hired worker. The schedule
form now has #117's box and question, and the fire adds the lines. This reverses #117 decision 8 ("scheduled hires
never add the lines") and #95 decision 4's "scheduled hires have no box". Code: `internal/proto/schedule.go`
(`ScheduleSpec.HerdrInstructions`, `Schedule.HerdrInstructions`), `proto.World.ScheduleHerdrInstructions`,
`internal/store/schedule.go` (`migrationScheduleInstructions`), `internal/server/schedule.go` (`fireSchedule`,
`applyScheduleSpec`, `scheduleView`), `internal/server/hire.go` (`hireLines`), `internal/server/hirepreset.go`
(`hirePresetCheckQuestion`); the game's `ui/scheduleForm.ts`, `ui/hireInstructions.ts` (shared with `ui/hire.ts`),
`world/schedule.ts` (`ScheduleBook.instructions`, `ScheduleForm.instructions`), `world/hirePresets.ts`
(`instructionsBlocker`'s wording); the fixture's `tools/fixture-schedule.ts`. Tests: `go test ./internal/store -run
ScheduleInstructions`, `go test ./internal/server -run 'ScheduleHerdrInstructions|HirePresetCheck'`,
`world/schedule.test.ts`, `ui/scheduleForm.instructions.dom.test.ts`, `ui/hire.ask.dom.test.ts` (unchanged, on the
shared module), `tools/fixture-schedule.test.ts`, `e2e/h127-schedule-instructions.spec.ts`.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wire and storage | `herdr_instructions` (bool, `omitempty`) on `schedule.create` / `schedule.update` and on the schedule's view (every `schedule.*` ack, the snapshot, `schedule.upsert`). Stored as `schedule.herdr_instructions INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` by a new migration (#62's is released): every older schedule is off. `schedule.update` replaces it with the rest of the spec. A handoff-only schedule may have it (the fire's prompt is then the handoff line and the lines). As #95 decision 2, the flag means "the current lines for the schedule's floor at its fire", never a stored text. |
| 2 | Older bridges | `decodeArgs` refuses unknown fields, and `herdr_instructions: true` in the snapshot only proves `worker.hire` takes the flag: a separate `schedule_herdr_instructions: true` (absent is not empty, #93 decision 9). Without it the form shows no box, never asks and never sends the field. The fixture plays one with `simfail=no_schedule_instructions`. |
| 3 | The fire | `fireSchedule` sets `HerdrInstructions` on the hire's args and goes through `hireLines`, the helper `hireTask` uses (#95 decision 1): the task is `schedulePrompt` (the late notice, the prompt, the handoff line, unchanged), the prompt is that, a blank line and `hireInstructions(s.Floor)`, in `a.Prompt` before `beginHire`, so `hireShape` checks the whole of it (size, Claude's typed check) and `compose` translates the task only (#39). The lines come once, last. `s.Floor` is the schedule's own floor (a virtual floor's `v-…`), never its base session. Run now and Retry go through `fireSchedule` and read the stored row. The audited args keep the task and the flag, as a client's `worker.hire`. The `hireWatch` callbacks and the stored prompt's secrets check (#108 round 2: of `s.Prompt`, not the composed prompt) are as they were. |
| 4 | Size | Save: with the flag and a prompt, `applyScheduleSpec` checks the prompt, a blank line and the floor's lines against 32 KiB and Claude's typed check (`bad_request`, "prompt with the herdr hiring instructions …"), as the bridge's backstop. A late notice or a handoff line that pushes a fire over is that fire's `bad_request` failure, as today: neither is known at save. The form blocks Save with `instructionsBlocker`'s reason ("…, the prompt is N bytes over 32 KiB. Shorten it, or untick Add herdr hiring instructions.") when it knows the lines. |
| 5 | The box | On a bridge with the capability the form has the box under the prompt, **off** for a new schedule (a follow-up's, a suggestion chip's or any prefill never ticks it), seeded from the saved schedule on Edit and sent as it is unless changed. The plain Hire form's hints, `dd-instructions` panel and collapsed "What's added" (the lines, "With them, the prompt is N of 32,768 bytes."). `hire.prepare` often fails for a schedule (an asleep floor): the box stays; "What's added" then says "The floor’s hiring instructions are added when it starts; herdr-world could not show them now." and the size check is the bridge's at Save. Ticking it never needs the classifier. |
| 6 | The question | #117's flow at Save: the secrets review, then (box off, `nudgeWanted`: the capability, `hire_preset.check` supported, the classifier `ready`, no `h3d_floor` in the prompt, not declined for exactly this text) `hire_preset.check` with `classifierView` of the reviewed text; only a "yes" in the client's 1.5 s stops the save. It asks **in the dialog**, "This scheduled task starts other agents (workers or subagents). Add herdr hiring instructions so they get their own workspace on this floor?", by **Schedule with instructions** / **Schedule without**, before a transcript reply is filed and before `schedule.create` / `update`. With: the box ticked, the size checked again (over: back to the form with the box ticked and the reason, nothing filed or saved), saved with the flag. Without: saved as is, the text remembered per form (an edit's schedule, a new one's floor) for the page's lifetime. Esc goes back to the form, nothing filed or saved. Any change to the form takes the question back; a "yes" for a form edited while it was checked saves nothing ("The form changed while its prompt was checked: …"). Enter held since Save never answers it (hire.ts's guard). An Edit whose prompt is the saved one does not ask: its saved choice stands. A no, an error, a timeout, `unknown_command` or a classifier not ready saves as is with no question; the box is only ever ticked by a click. |
| 7 | One copy | The box, the question's callout and the classifier call moved to `ui/hireInstructions.ts` (`instructionsPanel`, `askCallout`, `delegates`), used by the Hire worker form and the schedule form; `instructionsBlocker` takes how to name the task and the box's scope. The DOM and wording of the Hire form are unchanged (its tests and `h117-plain-hire-instructions.spec.ts` pass as they were). |

The threshold and bound are #95's. The lines themselves are unchanged: "every herdr workspace you create" already covers a recreated one. |
| 9 | Not changed | The dictated hire never sends the flag, and Hire orchestrator's `runPrompt` always adds the lines. A worker that ignores the lines still lands on its session's floor (#95 decision 9: a hint, not placement). |

## 2026-10-20 — #126 (parts 1 and 2): the transcript opens on a loading state, newest rows first

Opening a worker's transcript showed an empty overlay, or "No conversation yet.", for up to seconds while the 3D scene
froze: the client built every row of the watch's page and laid the whole timeline out in one task
(docs/research/transcript-open.md: 1.7 s on a 1,070-item Claude page with 43k elements, 37k of them diff lines). Part 3
(the bridge's outliers) is apart. Code: `game/src/laptop/transcriptRender.ts` (`backfill`, `Timeline`: `set`,
`slice`, `regroup`, `apply`, `buildSystem`, `ensure`, `opening`; `Transcript`: `holdBottom`, `room`, `filled`, `later`,
`drawDue`, `nextLazy`, `drawAll`, `rowShows`, `updateCounts`, `setLoading`; `diffLines`), `transcript.css` (`.tx-diff-body`),
`transcriptLoading.ts` / `.css` (the outline, in the main bundle),
`transcriptMode.ts` (`Sitting.acked`, `loader`, the `loading` and `frame` hooks), `laptop/index.ts` (the hooks), the
benches in `docs/research/transcript-open-bench/` (`browser.mjs` waits for the backfill and the diff lines, `app.mjs`,
`find.mjs`) and
`tools/fixture-transcript.ts` (`simtx=file`).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Telling "not answered yet" from "empty" | **The mode's ack, told to the view.** `TranscriptMode.reset` (the watch's ack, which every sit gets: `refresh` makes a new watch) sets `Sitting.acked`; the view mounts with `TranscriptRenderHost.loading` (`!acked`, or the ack's items not in yet) and hears `setLoading(false)` after the ack's `setItems`. A child's view is loading while its `availability` is null and hears it in `resetChild`. Items in the view end loading too. "No conversation yet." shows only when not loading, with no item and no pending prompt; a child's pending and unavailable words are ChildBar's as before. A re-watch's ack (`session_changed`, `resync`) never sets it back, and its `setItems` keeps the rows of unchanged items (row 5), so nothing flashes. Not `TranscriptWatches.ready` read by the view: the mode is the sink and already knows the ack per sitting and per child. |
| 2 | The three waits | One outline (`transcriptLoading.ts`) for all three: while the render module loads, the mode puts the screen's stand-in (`loadingScreen`: the strip's place, the outline, the prompt box's place) in the view's pane through the host's `loading` hook and removes it once the view mounts or the load fails; the view shows the same outline in its timeline (`.txl`, beside `.tx-empty`) until the ack; the first rows replace it in the task that builds them. An ack that came while the module loaded is put in a frame after the mount (the host's `frame` hook: `requestAnimationFrame`, then a timeout), so the mount and the first build are two tasks; the view says it is opening meanwhile. |
| 3 | The outline's look | A still outline of a conversation in the transcript preset's colours (`--tx-*`; the stand-in's strip and foot in the UI theme's `--ctl-*`, #216): the agent's lines, tool rows, your bubble with its corner, newest at the bottom (where the conversation opens; a short view cuts it at the top, the words stay), and "Opening Ada’s conversation…" (`role="status"`). Its rows brighten in turn from the bottom up, the order rows arrive in, by **opacity only** (compositor-run, it keeps moving through a busy task); under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it is still. Not a shimmer: `background-position` freezes with the main thread. |
| 4 | Newest first | A fresh `set` (no row to keep) builds the newest 30 rows **that show** under the prefs (a tool row "Hide tool calls" hides counts none, an image run counts once), then 15 more while they fill less than 1.25 views (a `scrollHeight` read each, 30 ms at most, also checked after each row that does not show), and sticks to the bottom: one cheap layout. Out of time with none that shows (a slow CPU, "Hide tool calls" on, many tool calls last), the view stays opening: the loader shows while rows are still to build, none built shows (`Transcript.rowShows`: the prefs, "Show system", a row looked at from the chip) and one still to build will (`Timeline.opening`). It is hidden in the slice that builds the first one, so the two paint together, and checked again when "Hide tool calls" or "Show system" changes. A page where nothing shows is blank as before #126, never "No conversation yet.". The rest are `pending` (oldest first, all older than every row built) and the backfill builds them from the end: **slices of about 8 ms (`backfill.budgetMs`, the clock read between rows, at least one row, at most 60)**, each one fragment prepended once, holding the place with an absolute target (`below = scrollHeight - scrollTop`, then `scrollTop = scrollHeight - below`, or the bottom while following; anchoring cannot add to it). **Each slice runs right after a frame is drawn** (`requestAnimationFrame` then a timeout), not on `scheduler.yield` alone: measured in Chrome 149, its continuations ran seven slices back to back in one 112 ms frame, before the frame's own work. A hidden page (no frames) yields with `scheduler.yield`, else a timeout. `data-building` is on the view while it runs. Not `requestIdleCallback`: the scene leaves few idle periods. |
| 5 | Rows kept across `setItems` | A row whose item is the same object or equal as sent (`JSON.stringify`) is kept where it is; only changed and new items are built. So a resync of the same transcript costs a comparison and moves nothing, and an older page (`older()`, `childOlder`, "jump to message") is built above in the background with the place held, which also keeps ChildBar's `loadOlder` hold right. With no row to keep it is a fresh start (row 4). |
| 6 | No whole-timeline pass per slice | Counts, tool counts, `failedHidden`, the jump chip and handoff lookup read the items (every item is in the `Timeline` at once), not the rows. A slice merges image runs only over the items from the oldest built to the end of the run it may join below (`regroup(list)`; a run that goes on into rows not built yet is merged again when they are), and runs no `afterChange`. When the last row is built, `filled()` syncs the handoff button, places the file popover and sticks once. A live `apply` still regroups everything, once per update, as before. |
| 7 | Live updates, a start over, going away | `apply` during the backfill: an item still to build is replaced in place in the queue (built as it is when its turn comes), a new one older than every row built waits with them (in order), anything else is built and put in as before. A new `set` (resync) and `destroy` end the backfill (a run number checked after each yield). `scrollToItem` builds down to an item the backfill has not reached (`ensure`), so the images tab's jump does not page older items in. |
| 8 | System rows | The view's timeline builds no hidden or unknown row until "Show system" is on (`buildSystem` then builds them in place; they stay built after). The counts come from the items as before. A subagent's nested timeline is built whole, as before. |
| 9 | Diff lines | A changed file shown open (#21's default, `data-changes="shown"`, its header and the call's counts drawn at once) gets its lines after its row: first when its body comes within a view of the timeline's (an `IntersectionObserver`, `rootMargin: 100% 0px`), and **once the last row is built, every other one** the observer reported away from the view, newest first, one at a time, so every line base drew is in the DOM again (review round 2: find in page missed the ones never scrolled to). Only reported ones: the drain's frame runs before the observer's first report, and a body in view taken at the far pace was laid out 500 lines a frame (h206's "Show the whole change": 3–4 tasks of ~55 ms); one drained that comes near goes on at the near pace. End on a body still drawing draws the rest of that diff first (as "Show next" does), so it reaches the last line (h171). One driver (`drawDue`) draws them, with `diffLines`'s `step`: per frame at most 50 lines of a body near the view (one 200-line diff laid out in 25 ms here: each line is a max-content grid), 500 in all, and `backfill.budgetMs`, the reader's place kept. A body whose row is gone (drawn anew, a resync) is dropped; a new one after the open (a live update, "Show changes" turned on, a file opened) is drawn the frame after. `data-drawing` is on the view until the last line is in. Until its lines are, the body is as tall as they will be (`1.5em` each, capped by its own max height). "Show next" says what it adds before the lines are drawn, draws what was put off first, and lines past its cut are never drawn, as before. `fileOpen`, `fileSet` and `diffShown` are unchanged. Without an observer (Vitest) everything is drawn at once, as before. |
| 10 | `content-visibility` | **On the diff body only** (`auto`, with `contain-intrinsic-block-size: auto` at its lines' size, set with them): a body away from the view is not laid out, so the drawing after the open costs no layout. Measured on the worst page (9,320 lines): the last line in at 337 ms with every frame at 17 ms, against 3.0–3.3 s at 50 lines a frame, or frames up to 106 ms at 500, without it. Find in page finds text in a skipped body (Chromium 149, `find.mjs`). Not on rows: they would need their own validation (anchoring, the bottom with estimated sizes, the strip merging). |
| 11 | What it costs | Find in page finds only what is in the DOM: rows the backfill has not reached and the diff lines still to draw (both a fraction of a second: on the worst page every row in ~0.1 s and every line in ~0.36 s after `setItems`), and hidden system rows before "Show system" (`display: none`, never found, as before #126). Once the open settles, every diff line base drew is found. |
