## 2026-10-21 — #149: the bridge keeps recently watched transcript indexes for return visits

A watch of a big transcript waits for its index to be built from byte 0 (`transcript.Follow` → `Ready`), and the usage
tracker closed a worker's log on the first round nobody watched it, so every return visit paid the build again. Now the
log of a worker (or child) whose watch ended is kept, still the tap of its session's one tail, and a watch of it again
gets it as it is: built already, with what was appended meanwhile. Code: `internal/server/txkeep.go` (the kept logs,
their events and `evictLogs`), `syncTranscript` and `syncKidTranscripts` (`internal/server/transcript.go`), the bounds
in `UsageConfig` (`internal/server/usage.go`), `Log.Stale` and `Log.Footprint` (`internal/transcript/log.go`,
`footprint.go`). Tests `internal/server/txkeep_internal_test.go`, `TestTranscriptReturnVisit`, `TestStale`,
`TestFootprint`; the hub-path bench `TestBenchReturnVisit` (`H3D_TXREUSE_BENCH`). Nothing a client sees changes
(`docs/protocol.md` untouched).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What is kept | The `txLog` the tracker had for the watch: the same `*transcript.Log`, still the session's tap (`SetTap`, `SetChildTap`; a kept child's native id stays in `WantChildren`, so its tap is not dropped and a Codex child rollout is still read). **No second tail and no second `Follow`** for a kept source: appends while away reach it through the tail that reads the file for the usage anyway. Its parse of those lines is the only work it adds while nobody watches. |
| 2 | Identity | The worker id and its tracker key (`harness/agent session`) for its own log; the worker id, the child's target (txKey) and `logKey()` (`harness/session/native`) for a child's; and for both the cwd the log was opened with (its path images' root). Another key or cwd closes a kept log; a watched log keeps today's behaviour (a cwd change while watched does not close it, it goes when its watch ends). |
| 3 | Invalidation | Closed, its tap cleared, and built again at the next watch: another agent session, another cwd, `Err() != nil` (the tail's `Void` on a truncate, a replace or the file gone), and **at reuse time an explicit check**, `Log.Stale`: `os.Lstat(path)` must be `os.SameFile` with the file the log opened and at least as long as what it read. The check catches what the tail has not read yet: a watch kicks a round whose first `syncTranscript` runs before the session's `Poll`. Each case has a test, with the change seen at the return visit and with a round between (`TestKeptLogInvalidated`, `TestKeptChildLogTruncated`). |
| 4 | Bounds | `UsageConfig.IdleLogTTL` **10 min** since the watch ended (a desk revisit within a working session; a deleted file's space and its descriptor are held at most that long), `MaxIdleLogs` **8** (one open file each), `IdleLogBudget` **16 MiB** of estimated footprint (row 6). Past any of them the least recently unwatched go first (ties by worker id and target); an eviction closes the log and clears the tap. Watched logs are neither counted nor evicted. Checked at the end of every usage round, and the TTL also when a watch comes back: a log past its TTL is never reused, even when the watch returns before a round has evicted it (the round's syncs run before its eviction); it is evicted (`ttl`) and built again (`expired`, shared with the eviction: `>=` the TTL; `TestKeptLogExpiredNotReused`, `TestKeptChildLogExpiredNotReused`). |
| 5 | The budget, from the measurement | The issue proposed a budget sized so the 220 MB Codex outlier's index is kept alone. **The index grows with items, not with bytes**: that rollout has 356 items and an index of **0.1 MB**; over every local transcript over 200 kB (1,019 files) the largest index is **1.03 MB estimated, 1.11 MB on the heap** (a 13.2 MB Codex rollout, 6,203 items); the next 0.84, 0.66, 0.63 MB. So no budget can single out the outlier. 16 MiB holds eight of the largest index seen twice over: on real data the count binds, and the budget only stops an index an order of magnitude past anything seen (one of 16 MiB or more is not kept at all; one of 8 MiB is kept beside a few ordinary ones). |
| 6 | Footprint | `Log.Footprint()` estimates the entries, their spans and ids, `byID`, the Claude message map, the open calls, the big lines' records, the resolved images (`memo`, `paths`, `hashLoc`) and the terminal sessions, at struct sizes on amd64, not the allocator's rounding. Against the heap the index frees when dropped (GC before and after, `docs/research/transcript-open-bench/open.go` now prints both): 0.252 / 0.277 MB (5.0 MB Claude), 0.104 / 0.118 MB (29.5 MB Claude), 0.091 / 0.100 MB (219.7 MB Codex), 1.033 / 1.105 MB (the largest): **8–12 % under**, the same order everywhere. |
| 7 | Not offered while kept | `offers` stays per watched worker and watched child, so a kept log produces no offer and does not hold the tracker at `WatchedUsageInterval` (1 s, gated on `len(tr.txOffers)`), nor turn on `WatchedRescan` (gated on the worker's watch, its handoff request and its watched children). Asserted in `TestKeptLogReused` and `TestKeptChildLog`. |
| 8 | Children | In scope, under the same pool and bounds: a child view closed and opened again, and a switch A → B → A, reuse A's log while it is its session's (`TestKeptChildLog`); a child of the worker's next agent session is another log, and the old session's kept children close. |
| 9 | Out of scope | **A worker gone from the round closes its kept logs** (its session goes with it; keeping them would need a tail the tracker no longer has). **A persistent index for first-ever opens** (after a bridge restart, or a transcript never watched) is a separate, larger change: ordinary first opens do not get faster. |
| 10 | Observability | Debug lines, ids and sizes only: `transcript log built` (`bytes` read before the tail, the running `reused` and `built` counts), `transcript log retained` (`footprint`, `items`), `transcript log reused` (`idle_ms`, `footprint`, `items`, `reused`, `built`), `transcript log evicted` (`reason` ttl / count / footprint / invalidated / gone, `idle_ms`, `footprint`, `items`). The hit rate is `reused / (reused + built)` from the last such line. `transcript watch read` keeps `wait_ms` (0 on a reuse) and `page_ms`. |
| 11 | Measured: the hub path | `TestBenchReturnVisit` on copies of real transcripts (this host, i7-10750H, 3 runs, ms; usage interval 200 ms, each visit after more than three rounds away). Cold is the first watch (the tail has read the file, as on a running bridge); "replaced" is the copy renamed over the file while away, which is rebuilt. |

| File | Cold `wait_ms` / `page_ms` | Return `wait_ms` / `page_ms` | Appended while away | Replaced (rebuilt) | Footprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.0 MB Claude, 1,326 items | 40–41 / 22–24 | **0** / 23–24 | **0** / 26–32 | 40–44 / 22 | 0.25 MB |
| 29.5 MB Claude, 494 items | 165–172 / 59–60 | **0** / 54–64 | **0** / 54–82 | 166–234 / 58–62 | 0.12 MB |
| 219.7 MB Codex, 356 items | 1,545–1,957 / 41–59 | **0** / 39–40 | **0** / 38–39 | 1,536–1,553 / 41–42 | 0.11 MB |

A return visit within the bounds no longer waits for the build (40 ms, 170 ms, 1.5–2 s here); the page read is unchanged.
**Ordinary first opens, and visits after an eviction or an invalidation, still build** and cost what they did. The timing
over the SSH tunnel (`pnpm perf:mac`) was not measured: the saving there is the same `wait_ms`, the tunnel adds its
round trips to both.

## 2026-10-21 — #139: a Codex worker is hired and woken on a chosen Codex profile, by its CODEX_HOME

#139 was written for a global codex-auth switcher. #136 (`docs/research/codex-accounts.md`) came back **NO-GO**: a
worker started on account B with one `auth.json` switched back to A cannot recover from its next 401 (a startup lock
and `WaitReady` cannot fix a dependency that lasts the worker's life), and a stored thread does not pin an account
either (§4: a resumed thread reports whichever account the new server loaded). #138 made an account a **profile**, a
Codex home folder with its own sign-in. #137 (`docs/research/codex-accounts-shared-setup.md`) found nothing blocking a
hire on the work seat (`configRequirements/read` → `requirements: null` on both real accounts; plan `team` fetches no
policy bundle) and listed what a fresh home lacks. So a worker runs on a profile by having `CODEX_HOME=<its folder>` in
every Codex process it starts. Code: `codexaccount.Service.Prepare`, `codexapp.Launch.Env`, `codexapp.ReadProfile` /
`ReadHomeProfile`, `herdr.Control.ExportCodexHome`, `internal/server/codexprofilehire.go`.

| # | Decision | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Prepare(ctx, key) (env, release, err)` | Resolves the key in the profiles as listed now and returns `CODEX_HOME=<home>`. `release` is a no-op kept for the interface (never nil, deferred on every path). The default whose folder is not there gives no env (Codex refuses a `CODEX_HOME` that is not; the limits probe's rule). An unknown key, or a listed profile whose folder is gone, is a `*NotFoundError` (with its name when listed). A hidden profile prepares: hidden only keeps it off the meter and out of the picker. |
| 2 | The default is today, byte for byte | No `codex_profile`, or the default's key: no env, nothing typed into the pane, nothing checked (`TestProfileHireDefaultIsToday`, and every #155 test unchanged). The key is recorded, so the seat can name it. |
| 3 | Env in every Codex process | Off the default: `export CODEX_HOME='<home>'` (fish: `set -gx`) typed into the worker's pane (`pane run`) before anything of Codex starts there, because `herdr agent start` takes no env (the attached TUI, a legacy hire, the embedded wake all go through it). The shared server's launcher sets it again on the server's own command line, inside the `bash -i -c` string after `~/.bashrc` (fish: after `config.fish`), quoted with the launcher's helpers (`TestLauncherCodexHome` runs both shells with an rc file that sets another one). The export is a new control shape whose home must be a plain path; a profile whose folder is not is refused at hire (`bad_request`), not worked around. |
| 4 | Confirm, never keep an id | After `WaitReady` (and the version check), `account/read {"refreshToken":false}` and `configRequirements/read` on the worker's socket, `initialize` with `experimentalApi` (for `workspaceRouting`). Its `workspaceRouting.chatgptAccountId` is compared with the same field from `codex app-server` on stdio with the profile's `CODEX_HOME` (run per start, not cached: a second or two). Stored: `confirmed` / `mismatch` / `unconfirmed` and why, and the plan (`codex_launch.account`, `profile_note`, `plan`); the email is never decoded and the id never leaves the comparison (`TestProfileHireConfirm` greps the ack, audit, snapshot, log and record). `account: null` fails the hire with "`<name>` is not signed in. Run `CODEX_HOME=<home> codex login` in a terminal." and stops its server, also when the `configRequirements/read` after it fails or times out (`codexapp.Account.Answered`: the reply stands). |
| 5 | Policy | `requirements: null` passes. A policy whose allowed approvals lack `never` or whose sandboxes lack `danger-full-access` (what herdr-3d hires with) stops the server and fails the hire with #137's words; no fallback to Codex's built-in server, which would meet the same policy. A policy that does not list one of them does not limit it. No `thread/start` probing (#137 item 2's downgrade is not checked). Same on wake. |
| 6 | Without its own server | The switch off, or a hire that fell back: Codex on the profile's home alone says signed in and the policy (`ReadHomeProfile`), the account is `unconfirmed` ("it has no Codex server of its own to ask"). Such a hire is recorded as a legacy launch with its profile, so its seat names it. Its wake: herdr's own resume takes no env and looks in the default home, so the floor's resume fallback checks the profile's home again as its hire did (a refusal or no sign-in: not resumed, the reason on its seat, `TestProfileLegacyWakeRefused`), then exports it before it types `codex resume <id>` (`TestProfileLegacyWakeFallback`). A profile gone meanwhile wakes it as row 7 does: on the default, with a new session and the same note (`TestProfileLegacyWakeGone`). Sleep backfills such a worker's session id by its folder in its own profile's `sessions/`, never in `--codex-sessions`, where a match would be another worker's session; a gone profile is not looked in (`TestProfileSleepBackfillsOwnHome`). |
| 7 | Wake | `resumeShared`: pane at its shell → prepare the stored key → export → server (with the env) → checks → attach (`TestProfileWake` asserts the order). A profile gone meanwhile wakes on the default with a **new** session (its thread is in the gone folder; another home cannot resume it): the record moves to the default's key, forgets its thread and says "`<old>` is gone: woke on `<default>`. Its Codex session stays in that folder, so a new one was started." The embedded fallback runs on the exported home and is checked as row 6. |
| 8 | Bare home | A folder whose `hooks.json` (or `config.toml`) does not name `herdr-agent-state.sh` runs no herdr session hook: herdr never learns the worker's thread. A shared worker on another profile whose thread is not known yet is asked for it by its own server (`codexapp.RootThread`: `thread/loaded/list`, then `thread/read` of each; only the one root, no parent and no `subAgent` source, not ephemeral; two roots or none: no answer, never a guess), each Codex poll while its server runs, through `noteCodexThread`'s rules (never another worker's; herdr's report still counts). So the bridge joins it and a wake resumes it (`TestProfileThreadFromServer`, `…Rules`, `TestRootThread`). While herdr reports no session, that thread is also the root the worker's Codex subagents are bound to (`Hub.childRoot`; the worker's `agent_session` stays herdr's): from the poll that learns it, on every refresh, and after a bridge start from the stored thread, also when the profile is gone (it is the worker's until a wake clears it); herdr's report, once there, wins. The usage tracker reads the worker by it, so its #25 subagents and their transcripts are the same thread's (`TestProfileBareHomeChildren`, `…AfterRestart`, `…ChildTranscript`, `TestUsageCodexProfileChildTranscript`). It does not follow a `/new` in the terminal (the thread is known by then). A legacy worker's is found by its folder in the profile's `sessions/` (row 11). The hire says what changes as a note, not a failure. Syncing setup between homes stays out of scope (#138 row 8). |
| 9 | Game | The hire dialog's "Codex profile" (Codex only): absent with fewer than two visible profiles or on a bridge whose `codex_profiles` lacks `hire` (the dialog as before, no field sent), else the visible profiles whose folder is there, the default picked, one not signed in shown and not pickable. The limits line shows the picked profile's reading. Presets keep the key (`hire_preset.codex_profile`); a gone one hires on the default with a note in the dialog and the editor, under the chips, and also with only the default left and no picker (the one exception to "nothing with one"). The seat bar's "Codex profile" line under the Codex server's names the profile by its current name (looked up by key) with what its start found; a Codex worker without one (hired before #139, or write-code's) "Runs on the default profile (`<name>`)". Nothing with one visible profile, but a wake on the default because its profile was gone says so. |
| 10 | Dropped from the issue | The hub-wide lock and "two concurrent hires are serialized" (nothing global changes; replaced by `TestProfileHiresAtOnce`: each hire its own env, in its own launcher and pane), the switch back, every codex-auth call, and the "token refresh after a switch" note (no switch, #136). |
| 11 | Sessions per profile | A worker on another profile writes its rollouts under that folder's `sessions/`, and the bridge reads them there: usage, transcript lines and #25's Codex subagents (`usage.Roots` per worker; the folder is in the tracker's key, so a wake on another folder reads afresh), the lookup by folder when herdr knows no session, and the transcript's generated images (that home's `generated_images` in place of the default's). Never in `--codex-sessions`: a profile gone (no longer listed, or its folder gone) reads nothing. Such a folder's `auth.json` is never read (#138 row 3), so its pricing's auth route is unknown (`usage.Roots.CodexProfile`). The default profile and workers from before #139 read exactly as before (`TestUsageCodexProfileRoot`, `…Images`, `TestProfileUsageOwnHome`, `TestCodexProfileAuthUnread`). The two-real-account acceptance (hire A on personal, B on work, sleep and wake B) is the user's. |
| 12 | Tests | `go test ./internal/codexaccount ./internal/codexapp ./internal/herdr ./internal/store ./internal/usage ./internal/server -run 'Profile|Prepare|Launch|Account|Control|RunsHerdrHook|RootThread|UsageCodex'`; game: `world/codexProfiles.test.ts`, `world/limits.test.ts`, `world/hirePresets.test.ts`, `ui/hire.profile.dom.test.ts`, `ui/hirePresets.dom.test.ts`, `ui/seat.test.ts`, `ui/hiredToast.test.ts`, `tools/fixture-codex-profiles.test.ts`, `e2e/h139-codex-profile.spec.ts` (390 × 844 and desktop, in the Quiet and Ubuntu UI themes: the game's UI has no light theme and does not follow `prefers-color-scheme`). |

## 2026-10-21 — the seated terminal never enlarges a narrow pane by itself (#175)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What is 100%? | **The whole grid**, whatever the pane's width: `viewport` at 100% is `cellGrid`'s fit, its cells kept to `CELL_ASPECT` (letters never stretched wide), centred, with bars at the sides of a narrow pane. The cells grow only by the user's own zoom: A+ / A−, Ctrl + wheel and Ctrl + = / + / − / 0 (70–200%, above 100% the bottom-left of the pane, following the cursor). The #74 width fit (`widthFit`, up to 2.5× for a pane under 0.7 of the screen's width, and `PaintOptions.fitWidth`) is removed, not switched off. Supersedes row 11 of #74 in part. |
| 2 | Why | The hidden multiplier made "100%" up to 2.5× (and 200% up to 5×) for a split pane, so a 60×40 pane at 1200×600 showed 19 of its 40 rows, and the size depended on the pane's shape. Resetting to 100% did not bring the rows back. Unused width at the sides of a narrow pane is the accepted price. |
| 3 | What stays | The #74 fullscreen zoom of the herdr tab (the bridge's `pane.zoom`, the usual fix for a split pane), the seat bar's "Split pane 60×40" chip, and the standing glance view (its own big-type grid, `GLANCE`). |
| 4 | Later work | The full-window seated terminal and PTY resizing (#176) keep this invariant: 100% never enlarges or crops a pane by itself, only the user's zoom does. `paint.test.ts` (`a narrow pane at 100% (#175)`) and `terminal.test.ts` hold it. |

## 2026-10-21 — #140: Auto picks a Codex hire's profile once, at hire: repo rules first, remaining limits as tiebreaker

#140 was written before #139 replaced the codex-auth switcher: its "account" is a **Codex profile** (#138, a Codex home
folder), matched by its stable `Key`; "the active account" is the default profile. Code: `codexaccount.Pick`
(`internal/codexaccount/pick.go`), `internal/server/codexautopick.go`; protocol "Auto: the bridge picks the Codex
profile".

| # | Decision | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rules before limits | An ordered list of rules `{match, profile}`: `github.com/<owner>/*`, `github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (compared, ignoring case, with the `origin` of the folder the hire was asked for: a worktree hire's source, not its new checkout) or a folder (`/…`, `~/…`, on whole path segments). The first that matches wins while its profile is listed, there, signed in and not hidden; **limits never override a matching rule**. One that is not is passed over with a note in the reason ("rule acme/* names work, which is gone"), and the next rule is tried. |
| 2 | Limits only break the tie | No rule: the profiles flagged "May be used for anything" (off by default, the default profile's too; it competes only when flagged), by what their latest reading has left in the plan's `5h` window (100 − `pct`; `reached`: nothing left), then `week`. A stale, failed or over-10-minutes-old reading is unknown (the clients' rule), and a known value beats it. Still tied, or nothing known: the default among them, else the first listed. None flagged: the default. |
| 3 | No quota hopping | Auto is resolved **once, at hire**, to a concrete key (`runHire`, before #139's prepare): `codex_launch.profile` never holds `auto`, and a wake (`resumeShared`, the legacy wake, the resume fallback) uses the stored key and never calls `Pick` (`TestAutoHireWakeKeepsProfile`: the readings changed, the worker wakes on its profile). Nothing ever moves a running or waking worker to another profile because its quota ran out. That is the line OpenAI's terms draw: one may not "circumvent any rate limits or restrictions". Choosing a profile for new work by rule, or by which seat has room, is not that. |
| 4 | On the wire | `codex_profile: "auto"` on `worker.hire` and hire presets (stored as it is on a preset), accepted on the terms of any other key (a Codex hire, a bridge with profiles); `codex_profile` absent stays the default profile byte for byte (#139's tests unchanged), so old clients, `run.start`, schedules and write-code's launches hire as before. The bridge advertises it (`codex_profiles.auto`); the view carries `rules` and each profile's `anything`. No folder is keyed `auto` (`~/.codex-auto` is `auto-<hash>`). The ack and the audit result carry `codex_profile_reason` ("Account: work (rule acme/*)", "Account: personal (most left: 72% of 5 h)"): plain words, never an email or account id. |
| 5 | Settings only | The rules and the flag are set in Settings → Codex profiles (`codex_profiles.set`: `{key, anything}`, or `{rules}` replacing the whole list so a new order lands at once; at most 32, checked on save, a refusal "Rule N: …" under its row). Stored in `codex_profiles_settings`' JSON (no migration: a row from before reads with no rules). **No flag or environment variable**, so nothing in CONTRIBUTING's configuration. |
| 6 | Manual wins | A profile chosen in the hire dialog or kept by a preset skips Auto (no origin read, no reason). In the game, Auto is the first "Codex profile" chip and a new Codex hire's (and a new preset's) default; a preset with no profile keeps meaning the default. With fewer than two usable profiles there is no picker and nothing is sent (#139's invariant). No live preview of the pick: the dialog's limits line shows no Codex reading while Auto is picked. |
| 7 | Tests | `go test ./internal/codexaccount ./internal/store ./internal/server -run 'Pick|Rules|AutoIs|CodexProfiles|AutoHire'`; game: `world/codexProfiles.test.ts`, `ui/codexProfilesRules.dom.test.ts`, `ui/hire.profile.dom.test.ts`, `ui/hirePresets.dom.test.ts`, `ui/hiredToast.test.ts`, `tools/fixture-codex-profiles.test.ts`, `e2e/h140-auto-profile.spec.ts` (390 × 844 and desktop, Quiet and Ubuntu; `h140-hire-auto-*`, `h140-rules-error-*`, `h140-rules-*`). The two-real-account acceptance (a work repo lands on the work seat, a personal one never does) is the user's. |

## 2026-10-21 — #167: a Codex profile shares the default's setup by links, and the bridge shows when it drifts

A new Codex home starts bare (#137): no MCP servers, no herdr hook, no trusted projects. Code:
`internal/codexaccount/share.go` and `drift.go`, `internal/codexapp/hooktrust.go`, `internal/server/codexprofiles.go`
(`startCodexShare`); protocol "Sharing a profile's setup". Research: `docs/research/codex-accounts-shared-setup.md`
and the #167 probe of Codex 0.163's config writes (pinned source plus throwaway homes).

| # | Decision | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Links, not copies, not a tool | Codex 0.163 has no include and no extra config path. Turning "Share setup with <default>" on links `config.toml`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md` and `rules/` (those the default home has) to the default's canonical path; that is a handful of `ln -s`, so no third-party CLI ([Ducksss/codex-profiles](https://github.com/Ducksss/codex-profiles) makes the same links but knows neither herdr's hooks nor the Settings rows). Copies would drift the day either side changes. `plugins/` stays per home (two homes would stage bundles into one folder at once). |
| 2 | `hooks.json` is a real file per home | Codex keys hook trust by `<canonical CODEX_HOME>/hooks.json:<event>:<group>:<handler>`, a lexical join (a linked `hooks.json` keeps the home's path), so each home has its own file with the default's commands (an atomic copy, the default's mode). Its absolute path into `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` stays: one script. |
| 3 | Plan, confirm, apply | Turning it on (and Fix) is a read-only plan first (`dry_run`): link, keep, replace (with the backup name), write, skip. The apply carries the names the person confirmed; the bridge plans again and refuses, writing nothing, when anything else would be replaced ("~/.codex-work changed since you looked; look again."). Anything replaced is renamed to `<name>.before-share-<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>` (then `-2`, `-3`…), never deleted or overwritten: every rename that must not replace is a no-replace rename (`renameat2` `RENAME_NOREPLACE`; `renamex_np` `RENAME_EXCL` on macOS; refused elsewhere), a backup name taken meanwhile takes the next, and anything else that appeared since the plan is left as it is and stops the share there ("Stopped: a new hooks.json appeared meanwhile: left as it is."; what is left is drift). A correct link is kept: sharing again changes nothing. Off replaces each link with a copy of its target (a file by temp + rename, `rules/` by a temp tree renamed in after the link is moved aside, since a folder cannot be renamed over a link) and keeps `hooks.json`. |
| 4 | Hook trust is seeded by Codex, verified | After a share the bridge runs `codex app-server` (stdio) on the default home, reads `hooks/list`, and on the profile's home trusts exactly the hooks whose `currentHash` (path-independent) the default already trusts, by Codex's own `config/batchWrite` (`hooks.state."<key>".trusted_hash`, `mergeStrategy: replace`, no `expectedVersion`), which writes through the link into the shared file. It checks with `hooks/list` and writes once more for a lost write. Nothing trusted on the default is never trusted here. If anything fails (no Codex, a timeout, still untrusted) the report says "Codex will ask once to review the hooks of work." This is the one write into the shared `config.toml`, and herdr never edits that file itself. |
| 5 | Concurrent writers | Codex resolves the link and writes the target by temp + rename (`resolve_symlink_write_paths`, `write_atomically`), so the link survives and the target's mode becomes 0600 (normal, not drift). There is **no lock across processes**: two homes writing at once lose edits silently (measured 35 and 37 of 120 writes lost in two runs, 0 of 60 from one process). Herdr's own write is single-shot and verified (row 4). Codex's own writes (trust prompts, plugin toggles) are rare; a lost one is asked again. |
| 6 | Skills via `~/.agents/skills` | Codex reads `~/.agents/skills` from `HOME` for every home, so a real skill folder in a home's `skills/` is drift ("skill infra is only on personal"); its fix moves the folder into `~/.agents/skills/<name>` after its own confirm and leaves a link in its place, refusing when the name is taken. That move is the only write to the default home. `skills/.system` and other dot folders are ignored. |
| 7 | Drift check | Read only, on the profile list the limits poller takes every 2 minutes while a client is connected (#138's gate; no timer, no file watcher), for each visible profile with sharing on: a link missing, pointing elsewhere, replaced by a file or folder (`sed -i`), or whose target is gone; `hooks.json` missing or its parsed, normalized commands differing (never bytes); a real skill folder in one home's `skills/` and not the other's. Kinds are stable ids, words are plain. `config.toml.before-*` files are ignored. The poller compares lists with their drift by value, and the hub publishes only a changed view. |
| 8 | No config value ever | Drift and reports name files, MCP server names (from keys only: the `<name>` of each key path that starts `mcp_servers.<name>`, found by a small TOML scan that skips every value whole, so a header-looking line inside a string, array or inline table is never taken; a file that does not scan names none) and skill names. Tests seed a fake `ALTERLAB_API_KEY` and assert it is absent from every report, item, note, ack and event. |
| 9 | Safety | Only a profile the service lists, not the default, whose folder exists, is written to: resolved from its key through the service's own list, never from a path a client sent. `auth.json`, `sessions/`, the SQLite stores, logs, `models_cache.json`, `.credentials.json`, `skills/.system` and the keyring are never touched. The file work runs off the hub goroutine and is serialized by the service. |
| 10 | Hire note | A Codex hire on a profile that does not share ("work does not share setup with personal: no MCP servers, no herdr hooks.") or whose shared setup drifted ("work's shared setup has drifted from personal's: …") says so in its report and toast, before #139's hook note. `codexaccount.SetupNote(list, account)` is the one place it is worded (the orchestrator start can reuse it). |
| 11 | Game | Settings → Codex profiles: "Share setup with <default>" under each other profile's folder (none on the default's, none from a bridge whose `codex_profiles` lacks `share`); the confirm list with backup names; the report under the row; a "Setup drifted" badge, the list, Fix and "Move to ~/.agents/skills". The limits meter marks the profile's row "drifted" and its panel points to Settings. |
| 12 | Tests | `go test ./internal/codexaccount ./internal/codexapp ./internal/limits ./internal/server -run 'Share|Drift|MoveSkill|SetupNote|SeedHookTrust|AccountEqual|CodexShare|ProfileHire'`; game: `ui/codexProfilesShare.dom.test.ts`, `ui/limits.profiles.dom.test.ts`, `world/codexProfiles.test.ts`, `tools/fixture-codex-profiles.test.ts`, `e2e/h167-share-setup.spec.ts`. A real Codex 0.163 on throwaway homes lists the default's MCP servers on a shared home (`mcpServerStatus/list`, no sign-in needed) and reports its hook trusted after the seed. |
