## 2026-10-21 — #176 part 1: the full-window seated workspace, an opened xterm 6 and herdr's terminal controller

Sitting at a worker opens an in-app workspace over the whole window; its terminal is a real xterm.js widget, and the
bridge owns the seated pane through herdr's controller so the PTY has the window's size and herdr's history can be
scrolled. Research: the issue's spikes, `docs/research/wterm-assessment.md`; ground truth for herdr 0.9.1's controller
was measured in throwaway sessions (release, refusal, scroll pinning, frame sizes, widths). Code: `game/src/ui/seat.ts`,
`game/src/laptop/{seatTerm,seatTermLogic,watches,index}.ts`, `internal/herdr/termcontrol.go`,
`internal/server/termcontrol.go`; protocol "The seated terminal (#176)".

| # | Decision | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Engine | **xterm.js 6.0.0** (already the monitors' parser), opened in the workspace, with the official **@xterm/addon-fit 0.11.0** (the grid of the area at a fixed font), **@xterm/addon-web-links 0.12.0** (plain URLs, soft-wrapped ones joined) and **@xterm/addon-unicode11 0.9.0** (`activeVersion '11'`: herdr's grid measures emoji and CJK 2 cells, combining marks 1, as Unicode 11 does; xterm's default Unicode 6 would shift columns). No Ghostty or wterm (the user's decision), no webgl, clipboard, search or serialize add-on (DOM renderer; no local history to search or serialize; OSC 52 reads would hand the clipboard to the pane). All MIT. The repo keeps no list of JS package licences (only `FONT_LICENSES.txt`), and the bundle strips their licence comments, as it already did for xterm 6 itself: shipping their MIT notices is left with the other packages' (not part of this change). |
| 2 | Layout | The overview's pattern: `position: fixed; inset: 0`, inside the HUD (so the toasts stay above it), the game behind it inert (the canvas and the HUD's other parts; never a dialog, a toast or a popover such as the limits plate), drawn at the covered rate (`OPAQUE_HZ`), focus restored on standing up, a clip-path grow out of the monitor (an opacity fade with reduced motion; never a transform: it would break xterm's measuring and mouse mapping). The seat bar became it: header (whose laptop, the worker's status tape, Terminal / Conversation / Images as three buttons, the preset and text size, Stand up), a notices line (question, Codex launch, read only), the content area (the terminal; the conversation and the images over it, at its size), the keys. No browser Fullscreen API. The limits plate has no gutter beside it: it steps away (Shift+L peeks). |
| 3 | One keyboard owner | The seat's hidden textarea keeps the focus (IME, paste, copy), inside the workspace, so it is never a dead target. The widget takes no key (`attachCustomKeyEventHandler(() => false)`), its textarea hands the focus back, `disableStdin` is on, `onData` / `onBinary` are never read, and the parser's replies (DA, DSR, DECRQM, DECRQSS, window reports, OSC 4/10/11/12 queries) are swallowed where they start (`swallowReplies`, tested against a real xterm). Keys stay `seatedKey` → lanes → `worker.keys` / `worker.prompt`; paste and its secrets review, image paste and #38's insert-before-Enter are unchanged (a paste landing on the widget goes the same way). |
| 4 | Font and grid | The font size is fixed: the preset's mono × 1.2 × the terminal zoom (A− / A+ / Ctrl + wheel / Ctrl+0 and the preset change it; a window, layout or DPR change never does). `document.fonts.load` before `open()`, `open()` once the workspace shows, a fit on xterm's first render, a `ResizeObserver` and a DPR media query after; the grid (40–300 × 10–100; a smaller area clips) is the watch's `control` grid and then a `terminal.resize` debounced 120 ms. #175 holds: 100% never enlarges a pane's text by itself (an owned pane reflows to the window's columns; a read-only one shows at its own size, and one bigger than the content area scrolls inside it: the wheel, the scrollbars, or the arrow keys once the terminal is tabbed to, a focusable region then; the rest of the keys still type). |
| 5 | Transport | `terminal.watch {control: true}` (no new watch command, so caps, pump, backoff and every end are shared with the observer), `terminal.resize`, `terminal.scroll` (wheel or `bottom`), and two connection-scoped messages: `terminal.control` (who owns the pane) and `terminal.history` (`pane.get`'s offset, read through the read-only socket client, a method added to its allowlist rather than a CLI per poll). One controller per connection. A control watch keeps its process: no restart for a new fps (so the seat stays at its fps while you read), a resync is a same-size resize (herdr answers every resize with a full frame), and a new controller waits for the worker's one being released (else herdr refuses it for its own predecessor). Stdin commands go through a bounded queue, at most 64 KiB each (herdr closes a client at 1 MiB). A full queue (herdr not reading for a moment) drops what the new command makes moot rather than refuse it: a size the sizes before it, the reset to the live bottom the wheels before it; a wheel is refused. The restore size and the release always reach a controller that is still reading: the oldest queued commands make room for them, and a controller that never reads them is stopped after the grace (logged). |
| 6 | Ownership | Never `--takeover`. herdr's refusal (`terminal.closed` "… already has an attached client …", exit 0) or a takeover makes the watch a read-only observer at the pane's own size, for good, said in the workspace ("Another client controls this terminal: it shows at its own size, and the wheel does not scroll it"); typing still reaches the pane (herdr's `send-keys` works while another client owns it). A controller that keeps failing (4 in 30 s) falls back the same way (`failed`). EOF without `terminal.closed` restarts with the observer's backoff. |
| 7 | Release | Every end writes `terminal.release`, gives the process 1 s, then stops and reaps it. Before the release the PTY is resized back to the pane's size before the attach (the session snapshot's): measured on 0.9.1, with no herdr TUI attached the PTY stays at the controller's last size after a release or a SIGTERM; with one, herdr restores the TUI's size itself. A SIGKILLed bridge cannot restore (the kernel kills the controller; herdr drops the lock). |
| 8 | History | Wheel and trackpad over the terminal → `attachCustomWheelEventHandler` (prevented, never xterm's arrow fallback; read only, left to the browser: it pans the pane inside the content area) → whole lines from the summed deltas, at most one `terminal.scroll` per 60 ms; herdr decides between its history and the application's wheel. Output while scrolled up does not move herdr's view and sends no frame, so the bridge reads `pane.get` after a scroll and every second while the offset is above 0; the "N lines up" button goes back to live. Typing returns to live: herdr's `pane send-keys` does not (measured), so every job on the worker's input lane first sends the controller an empty `terminal.input`, herdr's reset. The state (`ControlState.history`: offset, max, rows) is what part 2's scrollbar binds to. `scrollback: 0` and RIS + frame on every full frame: no local or fake history, also after a resync or a reconnect. |
| 9 | Selection, copy, links | Drag selects (xterm's own). Ctrl+Shift+C off a Mac copies the selection (`navigator.clipboard`; Chrome's own chord, the inspector, is kept from it); ⌘C on a Mac and the browser's copy are a `copy` event on the workspace that takes the selection; Ctrl+C is still ^C. Links: WebLinksAddon's handler and `linkHandler.activate` both go to `App.external` (`openable`: https only; `allowNonHttpProtocols: false`, no `confirm()`), on **Ctrl+click (⌘+click)**, xterm's convention: a plain click or drag stays a selection. A hover names the gesture in the tooltip. OSC 8 links are per row (xterm does not join them across a wrap; each row's part opens the same URI). |
| 10 | #74's chip | Hidden while the seat owns the pane (its size is the window's) and the tab is never zoomed on sit; shown in the read-only fallback, renamed **"Zoom herdr tab (split 60×40)"** / "herdr tab zoomed" / "Zoom unavailable" (it changes herdr's own screen, not this one). A bridge before #176 keeps #74's behaviour (the preference zooms on sit). |
| 11 | Limitations | Part 2: mouse clicks to applications (`terminal.mouse`, herdr ≥ 0.9.2; the bridge cannot read the app's mouse mode from the JSONL stream), paste through the controller's bracketed-paste envelope, a draggable history scrollbar. ZWJ sequences: herdr clusters a family emoji into one 2-cell grapheme, xterm's Unicode 11 table gives it several cells (`@xterm/addon-unicode-graphemes` 0.4.0 is experimental and not adopted): such a line can be shifted. Mac Chrome (DPR, ⌘C, ⌘V, ⌘+click, IME) and VoiceOver are the user's to validate by hand. No performance claim is made. |
| 12 | Tests | `go test ./internal/herdr ./internal/server -run 'Control|PaneScroll|ReadOnly|Watch'`; `make integration` (`TestIntegrationSeatControl`, a throwaway `h3d-it-*` session); game: `laptop/watches.control.test.ts`, `laptop/seatTermLogic.test.ts`, `laptop/seatTerm.test.ts`, `laptop/keys.test.ts`, `laptop/fullscreen.test.ts`, `ui/seat.test.ts`, `tools/fixture-screen.test.ts`; e2e `h176-seat-workspace.spec.ts`, and `m16-transcript`, `h74-fullscreen`, `h175-narrow-fit` updated for the workspace. |

## 2026-10-22 — #144: a usage event refreshes only what shows usage; no forced layout per event; no activity-only child.upsert

Every `worker.usage` ran the whole world-change path (~30 refreshes, the top bar, the plan-limits plate, the inbox and
its pings, the boards): 5–9 ms of main thread per event on a 60-worker floor, and seated (or over a screen dialog) a
forced layout per event, since the plate measured its tab right after the top bar's writes. Code: `world/store.ts`
(`Change.usage`), `app.ts` (`applyChange`, `applyUsage`, `cityOnce`), `render/office.ts` (`updateUsage`),
`ui/limits.ts`, `ui/inbox.ts`, `ui/hud.ts`, `world/limits.ts`; bridge `internal/childagents/registry.go` (`quiet`).

| # | Decision | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Who shows usage | Step 0 of the ticket, from the code: the looked-at worker's desk card (`cardOf`, `focus` only) and the top bar's usage total of the floor it shows (`Hud.setFloor`). The look-at bar's usage chip (`hud.setTarget`, per frame by key) and the laptop's context meter (`Laptops.frame` → `usageSeen`, per frame) read the store themselves; the handoff dialog reads `context_tokens` when it draws. Nothing else does: the city's desks and floor badges (`memberOf`, counts), Settings → Floors (`floorGroups`), the overview page and wall screen, the inbox, the plan limits, the boards, every dialog's `refresh`. |
| 2 | `Change.usage` | A `worker.usage` and nothing else: the workers whose usage changed, in no other set (so the floor list is not refreshed and the pings' early return holds); `null` for every other change. A snapshot, or a `worker.upsert` with new usage and a new status, is not usage-only and takes the full path. A usage event of an unknown worker is usage-only of nobody and does nothing. Every other event keeps every refresh it had. |
| 3 | `applyUsage` | The looked-at card is drawn again (`OfficeView.updateUsage`; another desk keeps the new view for its next redraw: a look at it, an away, a lean), and on a floor the top bar when a changed worker is on the floor it shows. No `statusDirty`, `planDirty` or `overviewDirty` (no status, plan label or overview row shows usage). |
| 4 | One city per change | The full path builds `store.city()` once for the scene, the walk inside a building (`syncWalk` → `buildingFor`/`buildingById`'s tint, `updatePlace` → `pinHere`), the top bar, the inbox's entries and its pings (it was up to three times; `needCandidates` per reader). The reader lives for one `applyChange`; the other callers of those read the store's city as it is. A pin that changes the lists (`syncWalk` → `WorldStore.pin`) bumps the structure version, which builds it again. |
| 5 | The plate places itself on a corner change | `LimitsWidget.update` (the world path) places the plate (corner queries, `tabFit`'s `clientWidth` / bounds) only after its `CornerWatch` (a dialog, the reading overlay, the seat and its glass's edge, a narrow viewport), a resize, the theme, a peek, a prefs change or the book's `known` flipping; and builds `limitsView` only when the book's version, the profiles, open or refreshing changed. Time alone is `tick`'s (30 s), as its doc always said: a stale crossing or an "ago" no longer also moves at a random world event. |
| 6 | Inbox chip and counts | `InboxChip.set` asks the corner only when the chip comes or goes with its rows (its own `CornerWatch` re-places it on everything else) and writes its count and labels only when they change. `Hud.setCounts` keeps its items when the counts, asleep and N's key name are the same. A screen dialog removed from the page while open (no `open` change) is not seen until the next corner change; none of the game's screens is removed that way. |
| 7 | `zoned()` | One `Intl.DateTimeFormat` per time zone, as `daylight.ts` does (the options are fixed, so the zone is the key). |
| 8 | No activity-only `child.upsert` | The registry compared whole rows, so a running child's every activity tick was an upsert (113 of 121 in a 120 s live dump, ~36 % of events). A child `running` before and after whose only change is `last_activity_at` now emits none; the row keeps the latest time, which its next upsert, its stop and the snapshot carry. An idle child's activity still emits (it is shown, `idle 4m`). Staleness: a client's copy of a running child's `last_activity_at` may lag the bridge's by up to that child's run; the game shows a running child's `started_at` (`childSince`), so nothing it shows is stale. Protocol: "When an upsert goes out (#144)". The 5 s per-worker usage throttle (`internal/server/usage.go`) is kept as it is. |
| 9 | Measured | Production builds of base (9a83f7b) and head on this Linux host (Chromium 149, WebGL2 via ANGLE/Vulkan), served side by side, 3 rounds interleaved (base/head, head/base, base/head), 3 bursts each (one changed `worker.usage` per worker, in one task). Handler time per burst, base → head: perf-floor60 in the city 271–301 → 0.5–2.6 ms, on its floor 281–306 → 7.7–18.7 ms; perf-floor96 on its floor 469–607 → 11–41 ms; perf-city240 in the city 1349–1461 → 2.2–6.7 ms. A burst is one task, so it is also the longest task (one head outlier: a 63 ms task in the first round's floor96). Seated at a laptop (demo-m5, `simusage=2000`): 135–157 → 2.6–5.5 ms per 18-event burst, CDP LayoutCount per usage event 1.00 → 0.00–0.04; over 10 s of the sim's cadence alone (80 world changes) 111 layouts → 34–36 (the frames'). Typing in the hire composer on perf-floor60 while every worker's usage changes every 250 ms, key → next frame: p50 845–1285 → 20 ms, p95 881–3218 → 22–51 ms, max 897–3857 → 27–55 ms. Probe: `~/.cache/h3d-144/probe/probe.mjs` (not in the repo); the regression guard is the e2e below. |
| 10 | Tests | `app.usage.test.ts` (which refreshes run, the city built once), `world/store.m5.test.ts` (usage-only vs every other change), `render/office.test.ts` (`updateUsage`), `ui/limits.dom.test.ts`, `ui/inbox.dom.test.ts`, `ui/hud.dom.test.ts`, `world/limits.test.ts` (one formatter per zone); `go test ./internal/childagents -run TestActivityOnly`, and the fixture end-to-end tests (Go and `world/children.frames.test.ts`) compare a running child's tree without its `last_activity_at` on the frames' side; e2e `h144-usage-perf.spec.ts` (@perf: seated, layouts per usage event ≤ 0.25, the total says the new sum). |

## 2026-10-22 — #146: start-up opens the socket early, defers unseen work, and draws the city shell first

Launch to a playable city was sequential: `await r.init()`, then the helper's bridge list and the font, then the `App`
constructor (which built things nobody sees yet), and only then the socket; the first city frame built every program
at once (66 programs for 74 draws in one 320–440 ms task here). Code: `game/src/net/startup.ts` (`startEarly`,
`socketUrl`, `applyBridgeList`, `handOver`, `FIRST_HELLO`), `game/src/net/preopen.ts` (`Preopened`, `firstPreopened`),
`main.ts` (`start`, `h3d.startup`), `app.ts` (`socket` option, `reception` getter, `stageCity`, `cityReady`,
`cityDrawn`), `render/arrivals.ts` (`kit`), `ui/settings.ts` (`renderSections`), `render/city.ts` (`BOX_PARTS`,
`setPart`, `furniture`), `tools/mac-runner.mjs` / `tools/mac-perf.ts` (`startup` job).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What runs side by side | **The renderer's `init()` and the helper's bridge list**; the socket opens as soon as the list settles its URL (`startEarly`). The font load stays after init: started first, it held init's own continuation ~100 ms on this host (the socket then opened at ~305 ms instead of ~205, and ready got later than base); after init it costs what it did before. The URL comes from one helper for the pre-opened socket and the game (`socketUrl`: `bridgeUrl` with the bridge scope, `none` for a helper without bridges), with the same inputs, so they match; if the game's URL differs anyway, the pre-opened socket is closed and the client opens its own. `open=none` only keeps links from opening a browser (`openExternal`): the socket pre-opens there too. |
| 2 | Who says hello | **The pre-opened socket, on open** (`FIRST_HELLO`: `helloFor(GAME_CLIENT, no resume)`, the client's own first hello), so the welcome and the snapshot arrive while the game is built. Neither the bridge (`readHello` first, `internal/server/ws.go`) nor the fixture server (its `greeted` gate) sends anything before the hello; the helper's proxy can refuse the upgrade (409 for a page of another bridge, 502 with the tunnel down), so the socket can close before the client takes it. |
| 3 | The hand-over | **Through the client's socket factory, for its first connect only** (`firstPreopened`). Until then the socket's open, every message in order, an error and its close are kept; they reach the client's handlers in a microtask after the factory returned, once `connect` has set all four (it sets `onopen` first). The client's own hello, the same text, sent on the replayed open, is dropped once: the bridge sees one hello. A socket closed before the take is a failed connect (backoff, a new socket). Reconnects, a resync, a bridge switch (`followSwitch` / `reloadFor` stop the client and reload) and `stop()` make and close sockets as before. A start-up that fails (the renderer, the `App` constructor or `start`) closes the socket nobody took (`handOver`), and one that fails before the list came never opens it. |
| 4 | What the constructor no longer builds | **The arrivals' figures and props** (built on the first walk, `Arrivals.kit`; nothing is drawn until someone walks, as before), **the Settings sections' content** (rendered when the dialog first opens, `reveal` too, every section at once and before anything shows, so a section that hides itself (`setHidden`, from the bridge's current state) is never offered; a section added after that renders at once), and **the receptionist** (built where it is first seen: a building's lobby as it is set up, `setBuilding`; the test hook builds it too). No idle prebuild: first use builds them, the same way whether or not anything ran before. Constructor, warm: 121 → 55 ms (Settings 30 → 8, receptionist 20 → 0, arrivals 26 → 0; measured with temporary `performance.measure` marks). The first walk now builds its meshes (~26 ms) in its frame; their shaders were built there before #146 too. |
| 5 | The city's parts | **The six box parts that precede the strips (`slab`, `wallN`, `wallW`, `kneeS`, `kneeE`, `pillar`) are one `InstancedMesh`** of 6n instances (part k of floor i is instance k·n + i), one white toon material and a colour per instance, drawn in the order the six meshes were. One program for the colour pass and one for the shadow pass, where there were six of each. **The mezzanine stays its own mesh**: merged with the six (the ticket's seven), it drew before the strips, bands and rugs, and one edge pixel of the demo city where its deck meets a window band came out another colour (in every shot, max 45 levels). Six merged: demo, demo-m3b and perf-city240 at noon and night, shadows on and off, pixel-equal to base (a frozen clock, the frame count as time, 0 pixels differ). The city takes no UI theme (`CityView` has no theme input), so one theme was shot. |
| 6 | The first city frame | **The shell first, the desks and figures compiled after** (`stageCity`, the first city build only). The first city frame draws the buildings, the ground, roofs and signs; the dollhouses' desks and figures (`CityView.furniture`) are hidden and compiled with `compileAsync` (picked while shown and unculled, then hidden at once; inside `holdDisposals`; `info.calls` advanced, as `warmUp`), then shown, their shadow pass built on that frame. **What the player sees**: the buildings appear without their furniture, and the desks and workers inside the dollhouses appear 150–185 ms later warm (535 → 706 ms here), ~280 ms later cold; afterwards the city is pixel-equal to base. Later builds (a floor added or moved) are drawn in one frame as before: hiding the desks there would blink them. Measured alternatives (same rounds as row 8): no staging, ready 662 ms with the longest task 321 ms (the same as base); holding the frame loop while the whole city compiles (no shell frame, the city appears whole at ~709 ms), ready 709, longest 84 ms. The shell variant was kept: it is what the ticket asks for, shows the city 175 ms earlier, and its ready is the same. `compileAsync` yields with `scheduler.yield` here, so only one or two frames are drawn while it runs. Precompiling the shadow pass would mean driving three's `ShadowNode` render function by hand: not done; that frame stays under 50 ms on the demo. **A cold ride during it**: the doors close for 280 ms, so on a slow start or a big city a floor's compile (`warmUp`, #141 row 6) can start while this one runs and end after it. The two holds overlap without nesting, so `holdDisposals` counts the running holds: `dispatchEvent` stays wrapped until the last one's work has ended (finished or thrown), and every `dispose` recorded since the first is fired again once, then; never while a compile that may still build the object runs. The city's disposals are released when the ride's compile ends rather than its own (harmless: nothing is drawn of them). Serializing the two (the ride waiting for the city) was not chosen: it would keep the doors shut for the rest of the city's compile. The frame loop's hold (`warming`), `staging` and `ready` are unchanged. |
| 7 | When start-up is done | **`__h3d.ready` waits for the first city to be compiled and drawn whole** (`App.cityReady`: a snapshot in, the furniture shown and drawn once), so `openGame`, `make shot`, the visual specs and `mac-runner.mjs` (all wait for `ready`) see the whole city. `__h3d.startup` records the first frame that drew the city and ready (`performance.now()`) with `renderer.info.memory.programs` at each. |
| 8 | Measured (this host, Chromium 149, WebGL2 over ANGLE/Vulkan on an RTX 2060; production builds of base `9a83f7b` and head served by `vite preview`; the demo fixture; interleaved base, head, head without the pre-opened socket, three rounds of one cold launch (fresh profile) and three warm loads each; load average 1–6; medians of the nine warm loads) | **Ready warm 810 → 706 ms**, cold 1145 → 1136. **The longest task from the first city frame to ready 329 → 153 ms** (cold 433 → 223). **The first city frame links 66 programs for 74 draws → 19 for 26**; programs at ready 66 → 57 (`shadows=0`: 40 → 35). In three's own counts (`renderer.info.memory.programs` / its pipeline cache, read through `__h3d.floorPool()` after each frame): base 83 / 67 at its first city frame, which is ready; head 32 / 19 at the first city frame, 73 / 57 at ready. The city's first pixels 810 → 535 ms. **The pre-opened socket alone** (head against head without it): 726 → 706 ms on loopback; through a proxy adding 40 ms RTT and an 80 ms dial (the helper's tunnel: base 878, head 751): 773 → 751 ms; at 100 ms RTT and a 200 ms dial: **956 → 873 ms (83 ms)**. Its gain is the handshake overlapping init and the constructor (the socket opens at ~208 ms instead of ~275–300), so it shows once the handshake is longer than that window, which #146's own constructor savings shortened. The proxy: a Node `ws` relay on a leased port that delays the upgrade by the dial and each message by RTT/2, the page's `?ws=` pointing at it (CDP network emulation does not delay WebSocket frames). The `@perf` specs that start in the city (`m3d-perf`, `h145-overview-perf`, `h141-floor-entry-perf`), base and head interleaved twice with `H3D_WORKERS=1`: all pass and match within noise (warm floor entry 66–68 → 59–65 ms, the first ride's longest frame shut 251–270 → 226–244 ms, the overview pages' idle main thread the same, the city 62 → 57 draws). `m3d-perf`'s second page (the city without logos) read 4.8–5.1 ms on base and 7.3 on head both times; benched outside the suite (with and without logos, four pages a browser, twice), head was at or below base on every page (2.7–7.2 against 2.8–8.0 ms), and the time follows how many pages the browser had opened before, not the build. |
| 9 | Measured: perf:mac (M2 Max, Chrome, WebGPU; `H3D_PERF_JOBS=startup`, base (a detached `9a83f7b` worktree with the new `tools/mac-*`) and head back to back, three rounds; each round launches Chrome twice on one fresh profile) | **First launch: ready 854 → 772 ms** (base 666–1054, head 654–793), **the longest frame until ready 208 → 76 ms** (base 127–259, head 75–80), the city's first pixels at 348 ms (347–387). **Second launch: ready 614 → 614 ms** (base 372–870, head 426–623), the longest frame 137 → 135 ms (base 132–207, head 126–138). Head: 36 programs at the first city frame, 73 at ready (`renderer.info.memory.programs`, WebGPU). The second launch is ready sooner on both (HTTP and code caches), but its longest frame is not shorter: nothing here shows Chrome keeping the pipelines across launches. |
| 10 | Tests | `net/preopen.test.ts` (with the real `BridgeClient`): hello on open, one hello on the wire whether the socket opened before or after the take, the welcome and snapshot kept and delivered in order, messages between the take and the replay, a socket closed before the take (with and without its welcome) as a failed connect then a new socket and a resume, the first connect only, a resync, `stop()` before the replay, another URL, `close()` before and after a take. `net/startup.test.ts`: `socketUrl` for the fixture path, `open=none`, the helper's bridge, `none`, the remembered bridge when the helper is late, none remembered; `startEarly` opening while init runs at the game's URL, the fixture and late-helper paths, init failing before (no socket) and after (closed) the list; `handOver` giving the first socket and closing it when building throws. `app.stage.test.ts`: the furniture picked shown and unculled, hidden while it compiles, shown after, ready only after a frame with it; a failed compile; no snapshot; a cold ride's compile started during the city's and ended after it still has its disposals fired again. `render/disposeHold.test.ts`: two and three holds in every order of start and end (nested, crossed, one after the other), each finished or thrown (744 cases), with a dispose before, after each step: each recorded one fired again exactly once, when the last running hold ends, none outside a hold, `dispatchEvent` wrapped exactly while one runs; a work that throws before returning a promise. `ui/settings.dom.test.ts`: nothing rendered when added, every section once on the first open before its `open`, later ones at once, `reveal`, a section hiding itself on its first render. `render/arrivals.test.ts`: nothing built before the first walk. Changed for laziness: the section tests that mounted a section without opening the dialog (`activity`, `appearance`, `codexProfilesRules`, `codexProfilesSection`, `codexProfilesShare`, `codexServer`, `promptSecrets`, `repoDiscovery`, `repoRefs` `*.dom.test.ts`) call `renderSections()`, what the first open does; `settings.dom.test.ts`'s render, remove/dispose, nothing-to-show and hides-itself cases open the dialog first; `arrivals.test.ts`'s props case starts a walk before it counts the meshes. |

## 2026-10-22 — #187: questions behind one glowing button, in one dialog that becomes a sheet, not pinned cards

The transcript view pinned its question cards between the conversation and the prompt box (up to `min(60%, 500px)`,
and on a short screen `fit()` gave a card the timeline's room), so the chat you need to answer was often out of sight.
Code: `game/src/ui/sheet.ts` (+ `.css`), `game/src/laptop/questionsButton.ts` (+ `.css`), `laptop/questionSheet.ts`,
`laptop/blockedCard.ts`, `laptop/askDrafts.ts`, `laptop/transcriptRender.ts`, `laptop/transcriptMode.ts`,
`laptop/transcript.css`, the `--ctl-q-*` tokens in `ui/uiTheme.css`, `input/shortcuts.ts` (`seat.questions`).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Where the questions go | **One sheet per transcript view, behind one button in the prompt box.** The ask's card (#57), the screen's question (the banner at the top of the view), the follow-up's (#90) and Codex's async questions (#157) are in it; the conversation keeps its whole height (no question sits between `.tx-main` and the prompt box at any size). The cards are reused as they were; only their way back to the timeline and their Esc changed (below). |
| 2 | One dialog that becomes a sheet | **`ui/sheet.ts`: one modal `<dialog>`**, a centred dialog on a desktop and a bottom sheet under `(pointer: coarse), (max-width: 640px)`, the switch in CSS only. The codebase had no bottom sheet; two components would duplicate the close paths, the focus and the key handling, and one keeps one behaviour and one test suite. It lives on `document.body` in the top layer, sized to the viewport, never to the laptop's screen (a phone's can be under 200 px tall). While open it follows `visualViewport` so the on-screen keyboard does not cover the focused field (simulated in tests, not tried on a real phone). |
| 3 | The lanes | **Mandatory (urgent): an ask and the screen's question** (the agent cannot go on; the bridge refuses a prompt). The ask wins over the screen's question, as before: one of them is in the lane. **Optional (calm): the follow-up's open questions and Codex's async questions** (Codex works on, user decision). With both lanes up the sheet groups them, urgent first, each under its name (`data-lanes`); this replaces the follow-up / async tabs (#157 row 10). The button counts an ask's questions (the screen's question is one), the follow-up's, and the questions on Codex's card (an answered one until it is cleared, so its reply state and Clear stay a click away). The sheet's accessible name is its lane's ("Answer to continue", "Open questions", "Codex asked", "Questions for you", or "Answer to continue, and …", titled "Questions for you" as each lane has its heading). |
| 4 | What opens it by itself | **A new mandatory question, once.** Its id (`ask:<tool_use_id>`, `screen:<the bridge's question hash>`: the same prompt in the same blocked spell, not the cursor) goes into a per-worker list in `TranscriptMode` when the sheet opens for it (or is already open when it comes), so hiding it (Esc, ×, the backdrop) leaves it on the button, and nothing opens it again for that id: not a re-render, a reconnect's snapshot, or standing up and sitting again. Kept in memory (the last 32 per worker): a page reload may open it once more (accepted). Recorded at open, not at hide, so standing up with it open does not reopen it either. A different id opens it again. **Optional questions never open it**: the button glows and its live region says so. |
| 5 | Not over the terminal | **It opens only while the conversation is the view on the screen** (`TranscriptView.setVisible`, from `TranscriptMode`: not the terminal, the images or a child's conversation). A question that comes meanwhile opens it once the conversation shows. Going to the terminal (Ctrl/⌘+Esc in it, "Answer in the terminal", any switch) closes it; that id stays opened for, so back in the conversation the button has it. |
| 6 | When it closes by itself | **The urgent lane's last question gone** (answered here or in the terminal, withdrawn), **or nothing left in it.** A card that sends the keyboard back to the timeline: its Esc closes the sheet; its last question gone puts the keyboard on the next card up (else closes); its controls off while its answer is on its way keep the sheet open with the keyboard on the dialog, so a refusal is read where it was sent. Closing returns the keyboard to what opened it (the button, the timeline), or to the timeline when that is gone or hidden. |
| 7 | The button's place | **A row of its own above the composer, inside the prompt form** (`.tx-qrow`), on every screen; there only while something waits; 4 px of room for its ring. The prompt box, off while an ask or the screen's question waits (open or hidden), says "Answer the questions first (button above, or in the terminal)". The transcript's `.tx button` / `.tx svg` resets skip the button (`:where(:not(.tx-qbtn))`, no specificity added), which colours and sizes itself. |
| 8 | Keys | **Q** (no modifier, not in a text field) opens the sheet from the conversation while the button shows (it replaces "digits and Enter from the timeline go to the pinned card": the digits do nothing on the timeline now, nor do ← → between the tabs). In the sheet the keydown stops at the dialog (the game and the laptop never see it); `QuestionSheet` routes it to the card the keyboard is on: the digits, ↑ ↓, Enter, Ctrl/⌘+Enter, Ctrl/⌘+Shift+X keep their meaning; Esc closes the sheet (it went back to the timeline); Ctrl/⌘+Esc closes it and goes to the terminal (the ask's and the follow-up's text boxes now let it through, as the async card's did). In the shortcut list and `docs/shortcuts.md`. |
| 9 | The backdrop | **`dismiss.ts`'s `sheet` policy** (a press and a click both on the backdrop), although the sheet holds typed text: what is picked and typed survives closing (row 10). Pre-accepted. |
| 10 | What survives | **Everything picked and typed**: the follow-up's (`FollowupDrafts`) and the async answers (`AsyncDrafts`) as before, and now the ask's picks (`AskDrafts`, per worker and tool_use_id, the same memory-vs-storage rule: storage only while "Review prompt secrets" is off, never for an ask with a secret question). Restored picks reopen at the first question still to answer (all answered: folded, Send next). Stored picks are read as untrusted and must fit the ask. |
| 11 | Colours | **Red for mandatory** (user decision: orange is Ubuntu's accent, sun already means "waiting for you", amber reads as a warning) and **a desaturated slate cyan for optional** (not the accent, not sun, apart from the status hues), told apart by label and icon too (a stop sign / a speech bubble). Tokens `--ctl-q-urgent` / `-text`, `--ctl-q-optional` / `-text`. Quiet: urgent `#ff7a72` with `#0b1020` 7.46:1, its ring ≥ 4.40:1 on every ground; optional `#88c4d0` / `#0b1020` 9.79:1, ring ≥ 5.77:1. Ubuntu: urgent `#ff5a6e` (hue 353°, apart from `#e95420` and the salmon `--ctl-error`) / `#2c001e` 6.16:1, ring ≥ 3.69:1 (on `#5e2750`); optional `#9cc8db` / `#2c001e` 10.39:1, ring ≥ 6.22:1. "Every ground": `--ctl-bar`, `-raised`, `-hover`, `-well`, `--surface`, `--raised` and both transcript presets' `--tx-bg`, `-bg-2`, `-bg-3` (`uiTheme.test.ts`, reading the real tokens). The urgent glow breathes, the optional one is still; static under reduced motion, paused while the page is hidden; system colours under forced colours. |
| 12 | The cards' CSS outside `.tx` | **The rules under the view's root that reach the cards (and its resets) are written `:is(.tx, .tx-qcards) …`**, the same specificity as `.tx …`, so the cards keep their resets, icon sizes, focus ring and Ubuntu rules in the sheet's `.tx-qcards` box. The `--tx-*` set is on the document root (`themeLoader`), so it reaches the sheet as it is. `.tx-qcards` is a container named `tx` (inline size) so the cards' narrow-width rules fit a phone's sheet; their short-height rules were the pinned layout's and went. |
| 13 | Removed (the pinned layout) | `fit()`, `fitsBeside()`, `data-tight`, `data-asking`, `data-followup`, `data-asyncq`, `data-front`, `SHORT_SCREEN`, `QUESTION_ROOM`, the `.tx-qtabs` tablist and `pickCard`, the `front` / `syncCards` ordering, the cards' `suppress()` (the follow-up and async cards no longer wait behind an ask: they are in the other lane), the "from the timeline" key routing, the top banner (`.tx-banner`, `renderBanner()`; its prompt-box half is `renderPrompt()`), and the cards' `max-height`, short-screen and `data-tight` rules in `transcript.css`. |
| 14 | Tests | Unit: `askDrafts.test.ts`; `questionSheet.dom.test.ts` (full height, the button in the prompt box, optional never opens, Q only outside a text field, names per lane, a hidden view, answered while open, a refusal keeps it open, nothing left after destroy); `transcriptMode.answers.dom.test.ts` (once per ask across a redraw and seats, a new ask opens it, picks across closing and standing up, never over the terminal, Ctrl+Esc, no dialog left after standing up); `transcriptRender.test.ts` (the screen's question in the sheet: once per hash, chips and digits, the prompt off open or hidden); `askCard.test.ts`, `followupCard.test.ts`, `asyncCard.test.ts`, `asyncCard.retry.test.ts` moved to the sheet; B's `sheet.dom.test.ts`, `questionsButton.dom.test.ts`, `uiTheme.test.ts`. e2e: `m16-ask`, `followups`, `h157-async-questions` (dialog and bottom sheet, touch contexts on a phone, the timeline meeting the prompt box with the sheet hidden), `m16-transcript*`, `h172-ubuntu`, `m59-themes`, `h124-fields`, the ui-theme audits. |

## 2026-10-22 — #190: the command bar resolves spoken model families and efforts against the models you see

The "Say a command" bar (#213) sent the sentence to `hire.interpret` (#211), which read it against the bridge's whole
catalog: "Please spawn a GPT Sol agent on high reasoning to …" asked "Which model did you mean by “GPT Sol”?" although
the user had hidden every other Sol in Settings → Harness models, and an LLM answer of "X high" was rejected as no
effort level. The interpretation now reads only the visible models, resolves a family and the spoken efforts
deterministically around the LLM's unchanged answer, and asks the classifier only about a near miss ("GPT soul").
Code: `internal/hireintent` (`visible.go`, `family.go`, `select.go`, `resolve.go`), `internal/server/hireintent.go`,
`internal/proto/hireintent.go`, `game/src/app.ts`, `game/tools/fixture-interpret.ts`; protocol:
[Hire interpretation](protocol.md#hire-interpretation).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility on the wire (D1) | **`hire.interpret {hidden_models?}`**: `{"claude": [ids], "codex": [ids]}`, the browser's `h3d.hire.hiddenModels`, sent by the game with every `hire.interpret` (new and follow-up) as it is when the sentence goes, left out when nothing is hidden (an old client: nothing hidden). The bridge reads its own catalog minus those ids (`Catalog.Without`: their `model_labels` and `extra_efforts` too), for the LLM's `hire_options`, the rules and every question's choices. It only removes: unknown ids and harnesses are ignored, a harness with every model hidden has none (named, it is `invalid`, as an empty one). Bounded by `CheckHidden` (8 harnesses, 256 ids each, 1-200 bytes of text each), else `bad_request`. |
| 2 | Revalidation (D2) | The bridge keeps nothing: every call re-resolves the whole proposal, pending fields included, against the current catalog minus that call's list. A pending model hidden since is `invalid` and asked among the visible ones, in the words first said (a pending model taken by family is sent back as its id; asked again, the question quotes the pending `said`). Review round 1 (F1): a pending **valid** model keeps its identity: it is checked by its exact id against the call's visible catalog (`keepModel`), kept while shown and of the harness said, else `invalid`; it never goes through the family rules again (it did, and an effort-only reply turned a hidden gpt-6.1-sol into the visible gpt-6-sol, ready). A pending invalid model's words go through the rules again. Round 3 (F1 reopened): whether a reply changes the model is read from the reply's own words outside the task (a number, a model's word that is no brand or glue, or a near miss of one: `saysModel`), never from the LLM's `model` being set, so an effort-only reply keeps or asks the pending id even when the LLM repeats a model (its words, its id, another id), and a reply that names one is a selection from its words alone (an LLM null there is `missing`). Round 4 (R3-1): a brand said as a model's ("GPT", "Claude" without "Code") and a word of the LLM's `model` said in the reply count as model words too, so "Use GPT Banana with high effort." is asked again (it kept the pending Sol, ready); a bare unknown word the LLM does not return ("Use Banana…" answered null) still keeps the pending model, like L1. `Catalog.Check` (worker.hire, settings, presets) still reads the whole catalog: visibility narrows interpretation, never what the bridge accepts; the review and `worker.hire` are unchanged. |
| 3 | A hidden model said exactly (D3) | Its id or label, every word said: `invalid`, the model question offering the visible models. Interpretation never takes a hidden model, and the classifier is not asked. |
| 4 | Effort aliases (D5) | `canonicalEffort` maps the LLM's answer before validation: "x high", "X high", "x-high", "extra high", "extra-high", "xhigh" (any case, spaces or hyphens) → `xhigh`, "maximum" → `max`. The #211 rule stays: the level or one of its spoken forms must be said outside the task span. An effort the model lacks asks with the model's levels and the existing wording, quoting the level ("GPT-5.6-Sol does not support “xhigh” effort."). |
| 5 | Families (D6) | Names are cut into words and versions (`nameTokens`: gpt-6.1-sol and "GPT-6.1-Sol" are gpt, 6.1, sol; claude-haiku-5-5 is claude, haiku, 5.5). The LLM's model counts only through the words the user said outside the task: none said → `missing` (a model word only in the task is never taken); a word of a model the user did not say at all (not a harness's, not a number, not common to every model of its harness, such as "gpt") → `invalid`, so an LLM that invents or normalizes to a name ("GPT Banana" → gpt-6.1-sol) is asked, not obeyed. Said as an exact id or label, every word said: that model (another harness's or a hidden one is `invalid`). Otherwise the visible models of the harness named (all without one) whose words cover every word said: one → `resolved`, `said` kept; several → `invalid`, the question's `choices` exactly those (an LLM that picked a version the user did not say is read as the family: "GPT Sol" with three Sols visible is asked, whatever id the LLM gave); none → the near-miss step. A version said must match ("GPT 6 Sol" is never gpt-6.1-sol). A family contradicting the harness named ("Claude Code … GPT Sol") matches nothing of it: asked, never substituted. Review round 1 (F3, F4): a brand alone names no model (`brands`: the harnesses' words and the first word every id of a harness of two or more shares, "gpt"): "Codex", "Claude Code" or "GPT" answered as the model is `missing`, asked among what the words cover, even with one model shown (it picked the sole visible one). And the LLM's words are not the only ones checked: `sayAround` adds the words the user said around and between them, in one clause of the latest sentence holding them, up to glue (articles, verbs, "agent", "on", "with", effort levels, the harnesses' words; "one" only away from other numbers). A number or a word of a catalog model joins the words said; a near miss of one joins as weak (the classifier's); any other word is unknown and the model `invalid`, asked in the user's words. So "GPT Banana" answered "GPT", and "GPT six point one Sol" or "GPT six Sol" answered "GPT Sol" or another id, are asked, never the visible Sol. |
| 6 | The classifier (D7) | `Select(ctx, cls, selection, models, efforts)`: one yes/no question per candidate, state `{"request": selection}` (the dictation without the exact task span, `selection()`), outcomes `picked`, `missing` (nothing to ask), `ambiguous` (candidates) and `unknown`. It runs only for a value the LLM gave that a word near-misses (one edit, three letters or more: "soul" for "sol", "medum" for "medium"), never for a field the LLM left null, never over a value the words settle, never with zero candidates (so "GPT Banana", "Dragon 99", "banana effort" and a contradiction never reach it, whatever it would score). Several near candidates the said words cannot tell apart (three Sols, "GPT soul") are asked without it. Not ready, failing or timing out: no pick, the field `invalid` and asked, never an error of the interpretation. `hireintent.Roles` gained `Classifier()`; `Run` attaches it only when its role is `ready`; `TestHireIntentUsesOnlyAIInterfaces` holds. |
| 7 | Thresholds and the question | **`PickScore` 0.3, `PickMargin` 0.15**, from the live matrix's tuning set (the issue's 12 sentences, three runs each, jev-preview, 2026-10-22). The question names the candidate by family and full name ("Answer yes if it asks for GPT Sol (GPT-6.1-Sol, id gpt-6.1-sol), spelled correctly or as a similar-sounding word; no otherwise."), the best of ten wordings tried on the tuning set only: the first one ("answer no for … another version") scored a correct "GPT Sol" 0.10 and "GPT soul" 0.09. With it, "GPT soul" scored 0.38-0.48, names said right 0.90-0.96, and the sentences naming no model or another one (omitted, "GPT Banana", the model only in the task) at most 0.15: 0.3 lies between. The issue's 0.5 would refuse every misheard name. Held out, never tuned on: "GPT Soul" 0.34-0.44 and "GPT sole" 0.47-0.57 in the pipeline, picked; "GPT Luna" (hidden) and the models-in-task sentence probed at most 0.08. The probes also show what the classifier cannot do: "GPT 6 Sol" scored gpt-6.1-sol 0.64-0.74 and "Claude Code … GPT Sol" 0.81-0.83, which is why versions and harnesses are rules (rows 5, 6), never scores. The margin applies only between two near candidates the words tell apart (rare); with one, its score is its margin. |
| 8 | Batching and latency | Candidates are pruned before any call: to the harness named, then to the models whose words cover the words said, near misses allowed (one candidate in every live case), so a call has 1-3 questions. More than `ai.MaxQuestions` (16) are cut into calls of 16 asked in parallel, bounded by `SelectTimeout` (2 × `ai.DefaultClassifierTimeout`) inside the interpretation's own bound. Live: a pipeline call p50 209 ms, p90 235 ms (9 calls; round 2: p50 185 ms, p90 365 ms, 7 calls); the probe of every visible model and effort at once (19 models and 6 levels: 2 calls in parallel) p50 419 ms, p90 515 ms. |
| 9 | Truncation (AC8) | **`MaxTokens` 3,000 and `ReasoningEffort` low** when the model's catalog says it takes low (`ModelReasoning`, as #60's follow-up extraction; else none sent, as before). The configured mercury-3 reasons at medium by default and spent the 1,400 budget on it. Dry run (`dryrun -extra e2e-phrases.json`, 78 cases) and the live matrix (`selectrun`, 22 sentences × 3), same code: 1,400 / provider default: 68/78, 10 truncated, p50 1,462 ms, p90 3,013 ms; matrix 25/66, 41 truncated, p50 2,768 ms, p90 3,671 ms. 1,400 / low: 70/78, 3 truncated, p50 1,102, p90 2,142; matrix 47/66, 16 truncated. 3,000 / low: 74/78, 0 truncated, p50 1,283, p90 2,359; matrix 64/66, 1 truncated, p50 2,361, p90 4,405. Earlier code, same LLM: none 67/78 (0 truncated, p50 632 ms, but it dropped tasks' final periods: no exact span), 3,000 / default 69/78 (9 truncated, p90 6,510), 6,000 / default 76/78 (1 truncated, p90 5,970, the costliest). As committed (3,000 / low through `ModelReasoning`): 74/78, 0 truncated, p50 1,161 ms, p90 1,904 ms; matrix 62/66 (tuning 34/36, held-out 28/30), 1 truncated, p50 2,076 ms, p90 3,477 ms. No prompt change was needed. Round 2, the final code, same settings, once: dry run 71/78, 0 truncated, p50 1,200 ms, p90 2,370 ms; matrix 61/66 (tuning 33/36, held-out 28/30), 0 truncated, LLM p50 2,218 ms, p90 5,138 ms. Every miss is the LLM's (an intent read as a hire with nothing in it, a final "?" or "." dropped from the task, one answer outside the schema, a model or an effort left null: asked); none came back ready when it should not, and none is the round's rules asking where they took the model before. |
| 10 | Prompt and schema (D4) | Unchanged: `prompt.txt` verbatim, the seven keys, the 50-case bench replay (`bench_test.go`) passing with the same expectations (its request check now reads `hireintent.MaxTokens`; the bench calls `Interpret` with no reasoning known, so no effort is sent there). Everything new is the deterministic and classifier layer around the LLM's answer, and the budget and effort of row 9. |
| 11 | A version said beside the name | The LLM reads only the visible models, so it normalizes "GPT 6 Sol" (hidden) to the one Sol it sees (live: `gpt-6.1-sol`, twice in three). A number said with the model's words is a word said too: "GPT 6 Sol" answered `gpt-6.1-sol` or "GPT Sol" is gpt, 6, sol, so gpt-6-sol or asked, never 6.1. Round 2: this is `sayAround`'s (row 5), which replaced the rule of the number next to a word; a version said in words is unknown, so asked. |
| 12 | The LLM's `selection_unclear` | The LLM flags the selection unclear whenever it cannot map a family to an id itself ("GPT Sol" is in no `hire_options`; live, about one in three), which left a found family not ready. The flag is set aside when these rules took the model by family or near miss **and** no word of another model of the whole catalog is said outside the task; it still asks when the model was said exactly, or with "GPT Sol or maybe Opus". |
| 13 | What stays (D8) | Intent handling, `multiple` (never a subset), cancellation, follow-up merging, the task as an exact source span (punctuation and later sentences verbatim), `ready_for_review` never launching, the review's confirmation, the secrets review (#108) of the sentences, no sentence in logs or the audit. |
| 14 | Behaviour changed on purpose | A bare family with one visible member resolves ("Opus", "Sonnet", "GPT" in the bench fixture's catalog, where Codex has one model so "GPT" is no brand: `TestContradictionsAsk` now expects those resolved). With the live catalog, "Opus" alone (five Opus versions) is asked among the five instead of whatever id the LLM answered. Round 2: "Claude" alone is the harness said and no model (`missing`, asked among its four; it was `invalid`, harness missing); a harness said in an earlier sentence still binds a reply that names another harness's model ("Hire a Codex agent…" then "Use Haiku 5.5." is asked: `TestHarnessLeftTheCatalog`), until a harness is said again. |
| 15 | Limits | A field the LLM leaves null is asked even when it was said (live, round 2: "GPT soul" twice and an effort once in 66 runs; D7 forbids guessing it). A version said in words ("six point one") is never matched: asked. A brand needs two or more models in a harness ("GPT" names the one model of a Codex with one, #190 row 14). `sayAround`'s glue is a list: a word it does not know next to the model's ("a shiny GPT Sol agent") is asked about, the safe side. Both harnesses said in one sentence ("Codex, not Claude Code") take no model. An LLM harness the user did not say, other than the model's family, narrows the candidates to none: asked. Round 1's limits L2 (a dropped harness) and L5 (a version normalized) are fixed (rows 5, 17). None of the 66 live runs came back ready when it should not, or with a model the sentence did not name. |
| 16 | Evidence | Fakes only in automated tests: `internal/hireintent/matrix_test.go` generates 4,800 model cases (9 ways to say the model × up to 8 LLM answers × 3 harness phrasings × 5 visibility sets × 5 classifier states, phrasing, effort and task rotating), 1,920 effort cases (10 spellings × 3 LLM answers × 4 phrasings × 4 tasks × 2 visibilities × 2 forms) and 6,875 follow-ups (every pair of visibilities between the sentence and the reply), each against an outcome computed from what was said and shown, the exact task span and `ready_for_review`; on the base commit (visibility simulated as the issue did, no classifier step) 2,259, 1,184 and 3,410 of them fail. Also `TestScreenshotSentence`, `TestSelect`, `TestNearEffort`, `TestSelectionUnclearAfterAFamily`, `TestRequestBudgetAndReasoning`, `TestCheckHidden`; the bench replay; `internal/server` `TestHireInterpretHiddenModels`; `game/src/app.dictation.test.ts` (the lists sent, following a Settings change); `game/tools/fixture-interpret.test.ts`; e2e `h190-command-bar.spec.ts`. Live (read-only catalog and AI config, no `worker.hire`, results not committed: row 11 of #211): `docs/research/dictation-hiring-bench/dryrun` (`-max-tokens`, `-reasoning`) and `selectrun` (the labelled matrix and the probes), numbers in rows 7-9. Round 2: the reviewers' reproductions (`review_test.go`, `deadline_test.go`); `property_test.go`, a no-substitution property over harness said (none, "Claude Code", "Claude", "Codex") × the LLM's harness (null, correct, other) × 11 ways to say the model (exact id, label, family, family and digits, family and words, a near miss, "GPT Banana", a harness word, a brand, none, "Opus") × 6 LLM answers (null, as said, a word dropped, another visible model, a hidden id, the harness's name) × 6 visibilities (one Sol, several, every Codex or Claude model hidden, one model shown, a one-model catalog) × 4 classifier states (off, failing, eager, high on every candidate but the one named): 15,792 cases, each checked against an outcome read from the case's labels only (never the package's helpers or result), the classifier never reading the task nor asked about a field not said; and 11,688 follow-ups, every pair of visibilities, the pending model kept iff shown. `TestMatrixFollowUpVisibility`'s oracle now comes from the first sentence's own oracle, never the result (13,750 checks). On 9941737 they fail: 2,665, 1,542 and 804. |
| 17 | A harness said binds (round 2, F2) | The harness is read from the user's words too: "Codex", "Claude Code" or "Claude" outside the task, in the latest sentence that names a harness (`saidHarnesses`), is the harness whatever the LLM's `harness` says, null included (the LLM dropped it on "Claude Code … GPT Sol", which then resolved to Codex, ready). Every path then sees it: the exact id, the family, the near miss and the classifier's candidates are of that harness only, so a model of the other is asked, never substituted; a harness said with no models shown restricts to none. Both harnesses said in that sentence: no model is taken (asked among every visible model). "Claude" is also a word of every Claude model: a Claude model said agrees with it. |
| 18 | The review asks the question (round 2, F6) | The Hire review's agent section shows the interpreter's `model` or `selection` question while the human has not picked a harness or model: its text (`rv-ask`, the chips described by it) and exactly its `choices` the catalog still has, grouped by harness when they span two (`agentQuestion`); one picked sets the harness and the model together (`pickAgent`), and the footer and the section ask for a model. A harness picked instead answers it with that harness's whole picker. "“…” is not in the catalog." stays for a name without a question; an ambiguous family's question now says "“GPT Sol” matches several models. Which one did you mean?". An effort said before any harness is known is held, checked once the model is chosen. |
| 19 | The bound (round 2, F5) | `Run` starts its timeout before the classifier is attached and the reasoning metadata fetched (`ModelReasoning` can wait for a shared slot and fetch the catalog), and `Interpret` makes no LLM call once the bound has passed: the 35 s cover the whole interpretation, inside the client's 40 s. |

## 2026-10-23 — #196: the MCP & skills wall reads configuration passively and starts servers only on request

The wall screen and its overview show, per harness, the MCP servers and skills configured for a floor's checkout and
Codex profile. The bridge part: `internal/mcpinv` (the reads, the checks and their cache), `internal/server/mcp.go`
(`mcp.inventory`, `mcp.check`, the worker observations), `codexapp.Watcher.MCPStatus`, `harness.Run` (the probe runner,
exported, wired into `mcpinv` by the app as its `Runner`: the hub reaches no harness package,
`TestCommandCatalogIsProviderNeutral`), the `expected_mcp` floor setting; protocol: [MCP and skills](protocol.md#mcp-and-skills); research:
`docs/research/mcp-skills-wall-display.md`.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Passive vs active | **An inventory read starts no MCP server and sends no turn**: Claude Code's config files and SKILL.md folders are read by the bridge itself (no process); Codex's are a fresh app-server's `config/read` and `skills/list` (they start no server). Starting servers is a **connection check**, only on `mcp.check`, never on a timer or on view; Codex's no-thread `mcpServerStatus/list` starts every enabled server on each page, so it is a check, never a read. |
| 2 | Unapproved project servers in the Claude check | Headless `claude -p` starts a project's `.mcp.json` servers without asking. The check passes every server not approved (pending and rejected) as `disabledMcpjsonServers` in `--settings`. Measured on 2.1.309 with an isolated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and fake servers: with the list an unapproved server never started; without it, it did; the `.mcp.json` of every folder above the checkout is loaded too, past the git root (the closest definition of a name wins), and the list excludes those as well. So the reader and the exclusion walk every ancestor to `/`, and a check is `skipped` when one of those files cannot be read. The `skipped` fallback for "the setting is ignored" was not needed. |
| 3 | Cache identity | `(harness, cwd, config home)`: Claude Code's config dir; Codex's resolved `CODEX_HOME` (the default profile runs without one, as a default worker does). A profile's answer is never another's. A separate cache from `harness.Catalog`, the same stale-while-revalidate shape, plus backoff (30 s doubling to 5 min), a 10 s first-read wait then `pending`, 64 keys. |
| 4 | User scope | Processes for user scope (no checkout) run in an empty private temporary folder: the bridge's home could hold a `.mcp.json` or a `.codex/` project layer. That folder still has folders above it (Claude Code loads their `.mcp.json` too, review round 1), so a user-scope Claude check also passes every `.mcp.json` server of those folders and of `~/.mcp.json` as `disabledMcpjsonServers`, approved or not; a folder free of them was not chosen because `/` or the home folder can hold one. |
| 5 | Audit | `mcp.inventory` is not audited (polled, reads configuration; also when refused), like `host.watch`; `mcp.check` is (it starts processes). |
| 6 | Worker observations | Only attached shared-server Codex workers of the floor in the asked checkout and profile, through their own thread (`threadId`: it reuses the thread's connections), at most once per 30 s each and only while `mcp.inventory` is asked. Claude workers have no control connection: their live status is not shown. |
| 7 | Display safety | By construction: the wire types have no field for commands, args, env, headers or URLs (a Claude server's command, args, URL and headers are decoded only to match the MCP policy, row 11, never copied out), and every note or reason is a bridge phrase (error text is reduced to a category). Tests marshal fixtures with secret-shaped values and assert none reaches a Snapshot. |
| 8 | Claude skills | Disk discovery of `<root>/<name>/SKILL.md` only (managed, user, project up to the repository root, enabled plugins), `complete: false`: no control request lists skills with their origin without reloading them (`reload_skills` is a state change). |
| 9 | Approval precedence (review round 1) | Measured with `get_settings` on 2.1.309: `enabledMcpjsonServers` and `disabledMcpjsonServers` add up over the scopes; `enableAllProjectMcpServers` is the most specific scope's (managed, `settings.local.json`, the `~/.claude.json` project entry only when `true`, project `settings.json`, user), so a local `false` revokes a user `true` (it was OR-ed, so the check started a server the user had revoked). `get_settings` does not show trust: per the docs the project's two files approve only in a trusted folder, so there they may only take approvals away (fewer approvals: the check never starts more). A matrix test covers every combination. |
| 10 | Failed reads (review round 1) | A failed state without an error (a refused RPC) and a Claude read that turns `partial` after an `ok` one are failures: the half keeps its last good rows, stale, and backs off. A `partial` read with nothing better kept is shown as it is and is no failure, else a lasting unreadable plugin manifest would freeze the half forever. |
| 11 | MCP policy (review round 1) | `deniedMcpServers` / `allowedMcpServers` / `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` and `managedMcpServers` follow managed-mcp.md: name, command line and URL pattern entries, deny first, the organization's servers need no allowlist entry. `${VAR}` values are not expanded (the policy's pinned environment is not the bridge's), so they never make a server `blocked`. The check also passes blocked servers as `deniedMcpServers` by name (measured: such a server, user or project, is then not started or listed), although Claude Code would block them itself. |
| 12 | Bounds (review round 1) | 64 keys including those in flight, 4 reads and checks at once: past them a request starts nothing (`pending`, or a `skipped` check not recorded) instead of queueing, since the client polls anyway. The checks of the last 30 s are kept apart from the evictable keys (at most 64), so eviction does not reset the cooldown. The Claude check's 20 s bounds the process too (it had 3 s more). |
| 13 | The overview's backdrop | The MCP & skills overview holds the typed expected-server list, so it is a `none` dialog (only its close button and Esc), listed in #51's table and in CONTRIBUTING. |

## 2026-10-25 — #198: Hire with handoff files the handoff, then hires once with its final path

"Hire with handoff" sits beside the transcript's inline Handoff button (same row, same candidate, shown only where
Handoff is). Step 1 is the filing dialog in a hire intent (`HandoffDialog.open(id, { intent: 'hire' })`); step 2 is the
reviewed hire (#212), whose one Hire files the handoff and then hires. Game only: the bridge, `internal/handoff`'s
`HireTask` and the cabinet's `hireTask` are unchanged (the cabinet's "Hire from handoff" and scheduled agents keep their
prompt).

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The task | `hireWithHandoffTask(path, task)` (`world/handoff.ts`): `First read the handoff here: <path> and then follow these instructions:` + a blank line + the task. The path as it is (spaces kept, nothing quoted). The task as written: only **blank lines before and after it** are dropped; its first line's indentation, inner blank lines, tabs and trailing spaces on its last line stay. Never the handoff's text, never the generic continuation. |
| 2 | Task and instruction | Two fields in step 1: the optional instruction (`ho-instruction`, what to put in the handoff, agent and LLM modes only) and the required task (`ho-task`, "Task for the new agent"). The task is not in the handoff plan (`HandoffPlan`) at all, so it cannot reach `worker.handoff`; it is the review's task box. Step 1 sends nothing but the existing previews; its instruction is reviewed for secrets when the review files it (the same flow the filing dialog uses). |
| 3 | Step 1 and a running request | Opened for a hire, the dialog starts from a fresh preview (literal, else the mode chosen when coming back) even while a request of the worker runs or failed: that request is the filing dialog's to show. The agent preview then says the agent can't be asked when it is busy. |
| 4 | Seeding step 2 | As "Hire from handoff" does: the source worker's floor and folder, its harness (else its agent kind) and model through `fromHandoff` against the current catalog, **no effort** (the review asks). The task's origin is "Your choice" (the human typed it), not "From the handoff". The desk is `hireSeat(undefined, floor)` before step 2 opens: a free desk, never the source's, also when it is sent home after filing. |
| 5 | The one submission | The review's `hire()`: its blocker first (effort, harness and model, folder, caps, task, and the size of the task with the fixed words and a path of `HANDOFF_PATH_RESERVE` = 1024 bytes: the bridge bounds the file name to about 100 bytes, the cabinet's directory is not known to the game), then the task's images, then `HandoffFiling` (`ui/handoffFiling.ts`, no DOM): `worker.handoff` with the plan's mode and one op, the agent's request or the LLM's job followed on the source worker **by that op only** (never `handoff.added`), `handoff.get` for the final entry. Then the composed task's exact size, the secrets review of the **composed** text (key `handoff:<op>`), the desk and the caps again (`resolveHireDesk`, `capBlocker`), and `hires.start` with key `handoff:<op>:<n>`. A new state, `filing`, locks the review while the handoff is made; its status line says the step ("Saving Pebble’s last message…", "Asking Pebble’s agent…", "The LLM (…) is writing the handoff…", "Filed <path>. Hiring…"). |
| 6 | Ops | One op per plan. It is kept after an unknown outcome (a timeout or dropped connection) and after a filed handoff whose path could not be read back: Hire again sends the same request, which the bridge answers with the same handoff. Any definite end (refused, failed, cancelled, closed) takes a new op for the next press. |
| 7 | Cancel and close | "Cancel request" (agent and LLM) sends `worker.handoff_cancel` and hires nobody; if the bridge refuses it (being filed), the review stops waiting and says the handoff may still be filed. Closing the review (Esc, Close, ×) while the handoff is made stops waiting: no agent is ever hired from that submission, the request keeps running on the bridge and files to the cabinet, and one toast says so ("No agent hired. <name>’s handoff will still be filed to the cabinet; hire from it there."). Reopening, another worker's review, or a late completion launches nothing: the filing ends once (`gone`) and every step checks the review's epoch. |
| 8 | After filing | The review keeps the filed entry. Every later failure (the hire refused or unanswered, a full floor, the desk taken meanwhile, the secrets review cancelled, a task too long with the real path) says `The handoff is saved at <path>.` and that Hire again hires only; the next Hire skips the filing and starts a new coordinator key. An unknown hire outcome keeps "look at the desk before you hire again". "Hire in background" is read once the handoff is filed: the review stays open while it is made, then the hire goes as any other, including #33's give-back (the given-back review keeps the plan and the filed path). |
| 9 | Not prompted | A hire created but not prompted: the coordinator's background path already holds the task it sent (the composed one) in the worker's Prompt (P) note. The foreground review closes on that outcome, so for a hire with a handoff it now does the same (`HireHost.holdTask`, the app's `PromptOverlay.holdTask`), and the toast says the task is in their prompt. No replacement is hired. |
| 10 | Back to step 1 | Before anything is filed, the review offers "Back to the handoff": step 1 again with the mode, instruction, send home and the review's task kept (the hire settings are seeded again on Continue). This is the way out of a stale literal reply or a mode that turned out unavailable. |
| 11 | No cabinet | Without a cabinet (`store.handoffs.known` false) the button says what the cabinet says ("This herdr-world has no filing cabinet: start it with --handoff-dir …") and opens nothing. |
